title: Joan Jett cancels remaining 2026 concerts after undergoing surgery for 'fractured vertebrae'
summary: Joan Jett underwent orthopedic surgery on a fractured vertebrae, forcing cancellation of her September shows including Bourbon & Beyond festival.
story: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel breaks down the symptoms of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus amid music legend Billy Joels brain diagnosis and why its under-diagnosed on Fox Report.
Joan Jett is stepping away from the stage after suffering a serious injury that required surgery.

In a since-expired post shared to Jett's Instagram Story on Tuesday, the 67-year-old rock icon's team announced that her band Joan Jett & the Blackhearts had canceled their two remaining scheduled 2026 concerts in September.
"Following a recent injury, Joan Jett has undergone orthopedic surgery on a fractured vertebrae and will begin the necessary healing process," the statement read, via Rolling Stone.
Joan Jett is taking a break from performing after undergoing surgery following a "recent injury." (Getty Images for Janie's Fund)
JON BON JOVI ABRUPTLY ENDS MADISON SQUARE GARDEN SHOW AFTER HEALTH SETBACK

"In close consultation with her doctors, Joan will not be able to perform at her forthcoming September scheduled shows in Costa Mesa, California, on Sept. 5 and Louisville, Kentucky, on Sept. 24," it continued.
"While Joan hates to disappoint fans, she will be taking this time to focus on physical therapy and healing. She's looking forward to delivering tremendous concerts for many years to come."
No additional details about Jett's injury were provided. Fox News Digital has reached out to Jett's representatives for comment.
The 67-year-old singer canceled her remaining two scheduled concerts for 2026.  (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for The Michael J. Fox Foundation)
The Pacific Amphitheatre in Costa Mesa, where the singer was set to perform on Sept. 5, shared Jett's statement on their webpage along with an update.
KACEY MUSGRAVES ABRUPTLY CANCELS CONCERT DATES FROM 'MIDDLE OF NOWHERE' TOUR
"While we understand this is a disappointment to all of you, we are happy to announce that Cheap Trick will be performing in her place, with X opening the show," the statement read.
"If you wish to attend the Cheap Trick / X show on Sept. 5, do nothing and your tickets will be valid. We look forward to seeing you," it added.
"If you wish to get a refund, please contact your point of purchase and we hope to see you at another show in the future."

Jett's concert in Louisville was scheduled to take place on the opening day of the four-day Bourbon & Beyond festival at the Highland Festival Grounds at the Kentucky Exposition Center. The festival's lineup includes Foo Fighters, Queens of the Stone Age, Mumford & Sons, Chris Stapleton, Kacey Musgraves and others.
Jett rose to international stardom after founding Joan Jett & the Blackhearts in 1979.  (Reuters)
Jett first rose to fame in the 1970s as a founding member of the all-female rock band The Runaways. She later found international success after she founded Joan Jett & the Blackhearts in 1979.

The band released 10 albums between 1981 and 2013, scoring major hits including "I Love Rock ’n Roll," "Bad Reputation" and "I Hate Myself for Loving You." Joan Jett and the Blackhearts were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2015.
In 2022, Joan Jett & the Blackhearts released their first acoustic album, "Changeup," followed by their six-song EP "Mindsets" in 2023.

Joan Jett & the Blackhearts have stayed active on the road since they first formed. In recent years, they have toured alongside artists including Def Leppard, Mötley Crüe, Bryan Adams, Alanis Morissette and Billy Idol. The band completed their first U.K. headline tour in 16 years in July.
Jett's team said that she is "looking forward to delivering tremendous concerts for many years to come." (London Entertainment/Getty Images)

title: 'Highlander' star Christopher Lambert hospitalized after collapsing at Steel City Con
summary: Christopher Lambert collapsed at Steel City Con reportedly due to low blood sugar and dehydration, but a representative says the actor is "perfectly OK."
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
"Highlander" star Christopher Lambert suffered a medical scare after collapsing at Steel City Con in Philadelphia during a meet and greet over the weekend.
The 69-year-old had to leave the convention due to a "personal issue," according to the event's Facebook page.
The French actor was subsequently taken to a local hospital by ambulance, according to TMZ.
Christopher Lambert collapsed at Steel City Con in Philadelphia on Saturday. (Getty Images)

A representative for Lambert told TMZ that the actor was "perfectly OK" and resting at his hotel. The representative said Lambert had not gotten enough sleep the previous night and had eaten little during the day, causing his blood sugar to drop.
Steel City Con representatives told People that the actor had become overheated and dehydrated.

"Christopher was feeling a little overheated and dehydrated. He had to sit down, but he is doing great today," organizers told the outlet.
A representative for Lambert did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
The 69-year-old was reportedly rushed to the hospital. (Getty Images)

The convention said Lambert was expected to return Sunday for scheduled photo opportunities and a noon Q&A panel. Steel City Con’s official schedule lists Lambert as appearing Friday, Saturday and Sunday during the Aug. 7-9 event.

Lambert is best known for starring as immortal swordsman Connor MacLeod in the 1986 cult classic "Highlander." He also portrayed Tarzan in 1984’s "Greystoke: The Legend of Tarzan, Lord of the Apes" and Lord Raiden in the 1995 film adaptation of "Mortal Kombat."

Lambert's representative told TMZ that the actor is "perfectly OK" and is resting. (Getty Images)

summary: A new photo with David DeLuise shows John Goodman looking nearly unrecognizable after years of lifestyle changes, weight loss and sobriety.
story: "Free Bert" star Bert Kreischer reflects on his weight-loss journey, sobriety and a series of life-changing events that gave him a new perspective on mortality.
John Goodman is turning heads with his dramatic transformation.
The 74-year-old actor appeared nearly unrecognizable in a new photo with fellow actor David DeLuise after the two unexpectedly crossed paths at a grocery store.
DeLuise, known for playing Jerry Russo on Disney Channel's "Wizards of Waverly Place," shared the snapshot on Instagram Thursday, showing himself smiling alongside a noticeably slimmer Goodman.
‘HOME IMPROVEMENT’ STAR JONATHAN TAYLOR THOMAS MAKES RARE APPEARANCE IN REUNION PHOTO WITH CO-STARS
John Goodman looks unrecognizable in a new photo amid his weight-loss journey. (Getty Images; daviddeluise/Instagram)
"He was my childhood!! Legend!" DeLuise wrote in the caption. "I love that I get to say that to someone ;), if you know you know."
Goodman's latest appearance comes after the "Roseanne" star spent years shifting his lifestyle and shedding a significant amount of weight.

The veteran actor previously revealed that he was approaching 400 pounds at his heaviest and had struggled for years with losing weight, only to gain it back.

Goodman has credited his weight loss to lifestyle changes throughout the years. (Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images)

title: 'Dallas' star Linda Gray reveals the bizarre way Larry Hagman avoided kissing scenes
summary: Linda Gray, who starred as Sue Ellen Ewing, shares wild stories from the "Dallas" set, including Patrick Duffy's surprise ambush and Larry Hagman's on-set pranks.
story: The actor, who was a sex symbol in the '80s, recalled playing the love interest of Brooke Shields and Linda Gray. Atkins now wants to work behind-the-scenes as a filmmaker.
Linda Gray is ready to kiss and tell.

The actress, who played Sue Ellen Ewing, the glamorous, famously troubled wife of villain J.R. Ewing on "Dallas," is teaming up with Julien's Auctions for "Ladies of the '80s," which goes live Aug. 12.

The sale gives bidders the chance to own costumes, props, personal archives and other rare memorabilia from some of the decade's most beloved television stars. It features two of Gray's original "Dallas" scripts from the episodes surrounding the infamous "Who Shot J.R.?" saga.
ANN-MARGRET, 85, REVEALS THE HABIT THAT KEEPS HER FEELING FOREVER YOUNG
"Dallas" aired from April 2, 1978, to May 3, 1991. At its peak in the 1980s, it was one of the biggest shows on television, (CBS Photo Archive/Getty Images)
Ahead of the auction, Gray looked back on her "Dallas" years, including the less-than-romantic kissing scenes she shared with her on-screen husband, Larry Hagman, who died in 2012 at 81.

"The first time we kissed, he had a mouthful of peanut butter," the actress told Fox News Digital. "I thought, 'Oh no.' And I had to keep going with this kiss. The camera didn't know what was going on. But here I was, kissing him with peanut butter. I almost killed him. I was like, 'You are so bad and very inappropriate, Larry.' And he didn't care. He just kept laughing. He thought that was funny."
Linda Gray told Fox News Digital that Larry Hagman wasn't a fan of filming kissing scenes. He'd often pull silly pranks to ease the awkwardness and keep everyone laughing. (CBS/Getty Images)

"And then it was onions," said the 85-year-old. "It was kissing him with peanut butter, onions, whatever he could find in a jar. That wasn't some romantic thing. On camera, it looked pretty good, but that was not my reality."
WATCH: CHRISTOPHER ATKINS LOOKS BACK AT ‘THE BLUE LAGOON’ AND ‘DALLAS’
Gray later discovered that Hagman wasn't a fan of on-screen kisses. Rather than endure the awkward moments, he turned them into practical jokes.
Larry Hagman died on Nov. 23, 2012, at the age of 81 in Dallas. (Gregg DeGuire/WireImage)

"He had told me quite honestly that he didn't like kissing scenes," said Gray. "And I thought, 'Well, we're going to be kissing a lot!' So when there was a kissing scene, Larry cringed, just cringed. He did not like it. But I think the pranks, psychologically, were his way of getting over the anxiety of having to kiss me on camera."
The "Dallas" set was notorious for its practical jokes, and everyone got caught in the crossfire.

Linda Gray (right, seen here with Larry Hagman) is offering treasures from her personal collection in Julien's Auctions' "Ladies of the '80s," featuring screen-used scripts, director's clapperboards, cast photos, awards, and more from her iconic career. Bidding is open now, with the live online auction taking place on Aug. 12, 2026. (Vinnie Zuffante/Getty Images)

"It was a daily prank, if you can imagine," said Gray. "And you never knew who it was going to come from. But it was mainly Larry. Larry was the prankster. I remember there was one episode where Sue Ellen was in the hospital. I was attached to all kinds of tubes and things on my wrists, arms and nose — all this hospital stuff. Larry came in, and he was supposed to talk to Sue Ellen. And Sue Ellen was out of it. She wasn't speaking, which was great for me."
Linda Gray's personalized director's chair, used while directing episodes of "Dallas," is estimated to sell for $800–$1,200. (Julien's Auctions)

"So Larry sits beside my bed and starts telling Sue Ellen how much he loves her," she shared. "Very soap opera dialogue. He's going, 'Oh, Sue Ellen!' and I'm lying there with my eyes closed, my eyes rolling underneath my eyelids. Then the door opens again. I thought, 'Who is in this scene that I didn't know about?' It's Patrick Duffy. He stands next to Larry and says, 'I did not know this was in the scene. Would it help if we sang that old song we used to sing?' Larry says, 'Yes.' And then the two of them started singing this very inappropriate song. I can't even repeat the words to you."
An original drawing created by Tony Bennett for Linda Gray is estimated to sell for $300–$500. (Julien's Auctions)

"I just burst out laughing," she continued. "The tube came flying out of my nose. I was totally blindsided. I thought I had ruined the scene, but everyone just started laughing hysterically. That was just how it was every day."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

From left: Patrick Duffy, Linda Gray and Larry Hagman pose during the 18th annual Screen Actors Guild Awards broadcast at The Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles on Jan. 29, 2012. (Kevin Mazur/WireImage)
Hagman's practical jokes were one thing. Facing Texas women in real life was another altogether.

"I was at a Dallas hotel for an event," she recalled. "I went to the ladies' room to put on lipstick. Next to me was this lovely lady with a little Judith Leiber bag. She opened it to put on her lipstick. I glanced down, and there was a gun in her purse. That was all she had in it: a gun and lipstick. I thought, 'Oh boy, I'm in Texas. Who carries a gun around?' So I said, 'Excuse me, is that a gun?' Really stupid, I know. She said, 'Of course, darling. This is Texas!'"

From left: Charlene Tilton, Linda Gray, Larry Hagman, Patrick Duffy and Sheree J. Wilson won the TV Land Pop Culture Award for "Dallas." An award presented to Gray is estimated to sell for $500–$700. (L. Cohen/WireImage)

"I had never been to Dallas in my life," she reflected. "I remember landing in Texas. Everything was beige and flat. I thought, 'I've got to know the women here.' And where do the wealthy women of Texas go? Neiman Marcus, of course, to get their hair done. And that's what I did. I remember seeing big, big hair. It was unlike anything I saw in California. These women dressed a certain way. Their shoes were always very stylish. And apparently, they carried guns in their tiny evening bags."
In "Dallas," Linda Gray starred as Sue Ellen Ewing, the glamorous, resilient and unforgettable wife of J.R. Ewing (Larry Hagman) on the hit CBS series Dallas. (CBS Photo Archive/Getty Images)
Gray got a crash course in Texas high society over one unforgettable lunch.

"One woman invited me to lunch, and she wore a special outfit just for it," said Gray. "I didn't have any friends in California who would do that. We're having lunch, and then she looks at her watch. She says, 'Oh, I'm so sorry. I have to go home. I have to fluff and fold.' I'm thinking, 'She has to do laundry? Fluff her towels and fold them?' No. She had to fluff her hair, put on her makeup and turn into the woman her husband expected."
Two of Linda Gray's original *Dallas* scripts from the iconic "Who Shot J.R.?" storyline are estimated to sell for $300–$500. (Julien's Auctions)
If learning Texas customs was intimidating, keeping the show's biggest twist under wraps was downright terrifying.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Linda Gray arrives at the Larry Hagman and Linda Gray VIP Preview Party at Julien's Auction on June 1, 2011, in Beverly Hills. (Tibrina Hobson/WireImage)

The "Dallas" Season 3 finale ended with one of television's most famous cliffhangers: J.R. was shot by an unseen gunman, leaving viewers to wait eight months to learn not only who pulled the trigger but whether he survived.

Gray recalled that the writers were searching for a jaw-dropping way to end the season with a bang when one of them blurted out, "Let's just shoot the bastard." After a brief silence, everyone agreed: "What a great idea. We'll shoot him."

Linda Gray is seen here as Sue Ellen Ewing in a scene from "Dallas." The Ewing family returned to primetime in 2012 when "Dallas" was revived on TNT. After three seasons, the reboot concluded in 2014. (United Archives via Getty Images)
As "Who Shot J.R.?" became a worldwide obsession, Gray found herself fielding the question everywhere she went, including during an interview with David Hartman.

In the "Dallas" Season 3 finale, "A House Divided," J.R. Ewing (Larry Hagman) is gunned down by a mysterious assailant, setting off the legendary "Who Shot J.R.?" cliffhanger. The mystery captivated millions of viewers and became one of the biggest pop culture moments in television history. (© Lorimar Film Entertainment/Courtesy Everett Collection)

"I was not very smart, but I said, 'Yes, I do,'" Gray recalled when asked whether she knew the shooter's identity. "'I know, and one of my children knows.' After that, I thought, 'Oh my God, I just opened Pandora's box. I thought everyone was going to call my house and one of my kids would answer the phone and reveal who it was. And then it would be all over.'"
The moment the interview ended, Gray said she rushed to call home.
Linda Gray's 1986 megaphone, signed by the cast and crew of Dallas, is estimated to sell for $600–$800. (Julien's Auctions)

"I remember telling my kids, 'Somebody's going to call you, and they're going to ask you who shot J.R. You cannot answer.' My heart was racing because it all could have been ruined. But nobody called, thank God."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Linda Gray still loves reminiscing about her years as Sue Ellen Ewing. Now, she's passing along some of those memories through Julien's Auctions' "Ladies of the '80s," where fans can discover memorabilia from "Dallas" and celebrate one of television's most decadent decades. (Paul Archuleta/Getty Images)
Decades after "Dallas" first captivated audiences, Gray said the memories were meant to be shared.

"I don't look at it as letting these items go," she said about the auction. "I look at it as sharing. There are a lot of people who still feel very connected with the show. And it feels good to share."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Tears for Fears star admits he fell in love with another woman before his wife died
summary: Roland Orzabal reveals in his memoir "Welcome to Your Life" that he fell in love with Emily Rath before his wife Caroline died of alcohol-related illness.
story: Matthew Nelson and Gunnar Nelson, the sons of late entertainer Ricky Nelson, have written a memoir, "What Happened to Your Hair?: How We Played Loud... Loved Proud... and Never Backed Down... Together."

Tears for Fears star Roland Orzabal is opening up about the painful final years of his marriage, revealing that he fell in love with another woman before his first wife, Caroline, died after a long battle with an alcohol-related illness.

The "Everybody Wants to Rule the World" singer, who has written a new memoir, "Welcome to Your Life," admitted he reached his breaking point after spending years watching his wife’s condition deteriorate. Orzabal described that while walking away may have seemed cruel, he eventually saw "a clear way forward."

"Why was it important to be so candid? Well, because it’s the truth," the 64-year-old told Fox News Digital. "I didn’t want to write something false. And also, I always felt that somewhere out there is someone who’s going through what you went through."
'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE

From left: Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith of Tears For Fears circa 1985 in New York City. Tears for Fears are best known for a string of ’80s hits, including "Everybody Wants to Rule the World," "Shout," "Head Over Heels" and "Mad World." (Robin Platzer/IMAGES/Getty Images)
"I’d spent years and years with Caroline in this state," Orzabal reflected. "It wasn’t just a year or six months. And yes, I had enough. I was shown a clear way forward."

In October 2016, Orzabal met writer and photographer Emily Rath while Tears for Fears were in Colorado to perform at Red Rocks. He wrote that his immediate reaction when he noticed her was, "That’s my wife."

"I’ve been around the world many times and had seen and met many attractive women, but I’d never heard those words before," he wrote. "They didn’t make sense, either, because I was already married, and this woman looked nothing like Caroline."
"Welcome to Your Life: Love, Death & Tears For Fears – An Iconic Musician's Journey Through Grief, Addiction, and Recovery" by Roland Orzabal is available now. (Dey Street Books)
Rath was 30 when she met the then-55-year-old Orzabal. "Ouch," he wrote. "If only I was half my age and she was older."

After exchanging numbers, the pair developed what Orzabal initially described as a "friendship between two creatives." Looking back, however, he acknowledged, "The truth is, I was falling in love with Emily before Caroline had died."
By then, Orzabal had spent decades with Caroline, whom he had known since they were teenagers.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Roland Orzabal's first wife Caroline. (Courtesy of Roland Orzabal)
Orzabal was around 14 years old when he first met Caroline Johnston. They married in Bath, England, in 1982, when the singer had just turned 21 and Caroline was 20. They had two sons.

Before Caroline’s physical and mental health deteriorated, the marriage had already endured significant strain. In the book, Orzabal describes a passionate but volatile relationship marked by frequent arguments. As his career took off, he spent long periods away and admits becoming increasingly "selfish," "hedonistic" and absorbed in his rock star persona.

By the mid-1990s, the marriage was in serious trouble. The couple discussed separation and sought marriage counseling. Orzabal says he was determined to keep his family together while acknowledging "the pain that I put Caroline through." Despite the turmoil, they stayed together.
British musician Roland Orzabal of Tears for Fears plays guitar during a performance at the Aragon Ballroom in Chicago on June 23, 1985. (Paul Natkin/Getty Images)

Things changed in the late 2000s, when the couple settled into what Orzabal describes as a predictable, day-to-day life where heavy nightly drinking became routine. Around 2011, friends began noticing a change in Caroline’s behavior.

"It was a slow process," Orzabal recalled to Fox News Digital. "She would say it’s menopause. 'It’s the menopause. I’m not eating because of the menopause. I’m weird because of the menopause. I’m depressed because of the menopause.' And she was always very emphatic, hard to argue with."
Roland Orzabal formed Tears for Fears with Curt Smith in 1981. (Courtesy of Roland Orzabal)

"I went along with this for many, many years until it was obvious that menopause was over, but the symptoms continued and got worse," he said. "It got worse and worse. We went to see several doctors, and they all said, 'It’s alcohol.' But even then I was in denial because I was a wine drinker. I thought, 'It isn’t doing me any harm, so why is it doing harm to her?'"
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Roland Orzabal married his first wife, Caroline Johnston, in 1982. The wedding took place around the same time his band Tears for Fears released their debut single "Mad World." (Pam Springsteen)
"To be honest with you, it wasn’t until the autopsy that I realized the truth," Orzabal admitted. "Terrible."

According to Orzabal, Caroline eventually struggled to eat solid food even as she continued drinking. She spent increasing amounts of time on the sofa, became anxious, stopped regularly cooking for their sons and alienated friends. Orzabal writes that her condition escalated to "seizures and hospitalizations," "bizarre ideation" and loss of normal bodily control. He described watching helplessly as she "slowly melted away."
According to the book, Roland Orzabal wrote, "Please Be Happy" about Caroline’s depression and deteriorating condition. (Pam Springsteen)

Orzabal writes that Caroline’s drinking became increasingly secretive, and he later discovered that she had been hiding bottles of vodka. He recalled seeing her jaundiced with "deathly red marks" on her face.
Roland Orzabal of Tears for Fears performs at Koninklijk Circus in Brussels, Belgium, on April 21, 1985. (Gie Knaeps/Getty Images)

"How much of a carer are you? Is that your natural bent?" Orzabal told Fox News Digital. "I would say with me, it probably wasn’t, but I did it anyway. And I think what it did was it would make me very angry inside, which wasn’t good. I had people talk to me about just leaving, which I would never have done. But I think in hindsight, it’s stupid to say now, but maybe I should have done something about it earlier or left. Sounds harsh."
Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith of Tears for Fears arrive at the German Radio Award 2022 ceremony in Hamburg, Germany, on Sept. 8, 2022. (dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images)
"I think the problem was that, one minute, she’d be fine," said Orzabal. "We would have a decent conversation. And then the next minute. She was doolally — not making sense, demented."
Orzabal wrote that as his feelings for Rath developed, he found himself confronting a choice about his future.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Roland Orzabal and his first wife, Caroline Johnston, had two children together: sons Pascal and Raoul. (Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)

"I was at a crossroads, a tipping point, if you like," wrote Orzabal. "A tipping point that would redefine my life. With all the things that were going on with Caroline, with all the visits to psychiatrists, to neurologists, to hepatologists, I was falling in love with a young, healthy woman who I believed loved me too and was the opposite of what I had left at home.
Tears for Fears at the Shepherd’s Bush Empire 2022. (Emily Rath Orzabal)

"... I had a talk with myself, out loud, pacing the room like some crazy man. I knew what was going to happen to Caroline: She would once again be committed and the whole process, the whole nightmare, would start again. And where would it end? I could choose the scenario, the illness, the misery and the frustration, or I could choose an alternative and leave her madness behind. ... I could choose life, or I could choose death. God strike me down, cancel me, whatever, but I chose life."
Orzabal told Fox News Digital that imagining a life beyond his wife’s illness left him with an agonizing sense of guilt.
Singer Roland Orzabal of Tears for Fears performs onstage during The Darker Waves Festival in Huntington Beach, California, on Nov. 18, 2023. (Scott Dudelson/WireImage)

"If you choose life at this moment, you were cruel," he said. "But I think it was the final straw because Caroline had already spent three months in a psych ward. I’d been there virtually every day going to visit her. And then, all of a sudden, that night I saw an alternative life for myself, which is hard to do — hard to take. But I did."
In 2017, Orzabal’s first wife of 35 years died. She was 54.
"I felt belief and disbelief," he said. "I couldn’t take it in because you have to go into action. I had to speak to my sons, my family. You’re clearing up the mess that death leaves."
WATCH: NELSON TWINS REFLECT ON FAMILY LEGACY AND THE TRUE COST OF FAME
In 2019, Orzabal said he entered InnerBalance, a rehabilitation center in Colorado, for treatment of his Ambien addiction. He said he began to forgive himself there.

"There’s this madness that comes with grief," he explained. "There’s the negotiation. 'What if I did this?' 'What if I did that?' And then, what happens when you no longer have that person to negotiate with? You no longer have that person to get angry. That’s all gone, and you are only left with the feeling."
Roland Orzabal's first wife, Caroline, died in July 2017 at the age of 54. According to multiple reports, she developed alcohol-related dementia. (Courtesy of Roland Orzabal.)

"I left out a lot of details, especially when it came to Caroline," he continued. "It was a lot worse, but I wanted to be respectful of those who’ve passed on. I wanted to respect her name. She’s my sons’ mother. So no, I couldn’t put the gruesome details at all. Even though it sounds bad, it’s much worse."
Roland Orzabal and Emily Rath on their wedding day. (Tara Marolda)
Orzabal and Rath married in 2020. They had a daughter, Eula, in 2025.

"Emily has been an amazing support system for me," said Orzabal. "It depends on your belief system - I think that if you believe in the soul, then [Caroline] would completely understand. When I think about the person she was ... she would understand."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Scott Eastwood says his father sent Kevin Costner home from set while filming 'A Perfect World'
summary: Scott Eastwood reveals on "Armchair Expert" how Clint Eastwood calmly sent Kevin Costner home from the "Perfect World" set after a trailer standoff.
story: The actor bought his dad a Silverado truck for Christmas once he found success as an actor.
Scott Eastwood is getting candid about how his father once asked a well-known actor to leave a movie set.

During a recent interview on the "Armchair Expert" podcast, the 40-year-old actor shared that everybody has "a lot of respect" for his father, Clint Eastwood, on set and that he "didn't raise his voice ever" while on set.

He then shared a "legendary story" about when his father worked with Kevin Costner and how he reacted when the actor wouldn't leave his trailer, noting "I’m sort of going to paraphrase it, and I’ll probably tell it a little wrong."

"Kevin Costner sort of going through maybe, the Kevin Costner rise to fame and maybe got a big ego, you know, blah blah blah, but they were doing 'Perfect World,'" he said. "Apparently, he didn't want to come out of his trailer for some reason."
Scott Eastwood said his dad never raised his voice while on set. (Aitor Rosas Sune/WWD via Getty Images)
GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'
Scott said Clint — who directed and starred in the film — reacted by saying, "Well send him home then," even though Costner was scheduled to be in the scene they were working on that day.

"So he sent him home, and I guess they just went to Kevin and said, 'Hey, you're going to go home for the day,'" Scott explained. "He said, 'What do you mean I'm in the scene?' You know, 'Well, I guess you're not anymore. Clint changed that.'"
After he was asked to leave the set that day, Scott noted, "I think the next day he was on set ready to go."
Fox News Digital reached out to representatives for Costner for comment.
Scott Eastwood said his dad once asked Kevin Costner to leave a movie set because he wouldn't come out of his trailer. (Getty Images)

"A Perfect World" stars Costner as an escaped convict who kidnaps a young child, with Clint playing the role of a Texas ranger who is searching for Costner and the young boy.

"I think I was lucky in some ways because I got to see it growing up and got to see like how it's bulls---," he said on an episode of "The Joe Rogan Experience," in June of certain behaviors on modern movie sets.

While Eastwood said he got a peek at bad behavior on set when he was younger and visiting his iconic dad on set, the "Wrath of Man" star said his father "did a really good job of protecting" him and his siblings from the pitfalls that come with child stardom.

Scott credits growing up on film sets with his dad for opening his eyes to what is and isn't acceptable behavior on set. (E. Charbonneau/WireImage for Lionsgate)

title: Tori Spelling poses in racy bikini top as she addresses departure from Jennie Garth's podcast
summary: Tori Spelling shared a bikini photo after confirming her departure from the "Beverly Hills, 90210" rewatch podcast with Jennie Garth.
story: The 52-year-old actor shares how the former co-stars managed to mend their friendship after nearly two decades.
Tori Spelling is taking an "intermission" while navigating a new chapter in her life and career.
The 53-year-old actress shared a new photo of her posing outdoors in a black halter-style bikini top and oversized denim shorts.
The "90210" alum accessorized with layered gold necklaces, oversized black sunglasses and green sandals as she stood on a sunlit wooden deck surrounded by trees and distant hills.
"Intermission," she captioned the post.
TORI SPELLING LIVING IN A 'BORDERLINE HOARDER' HOME AS LIVING CONDITIONS WORSEN
Tori Spelling rose to fame playing Donna Martin on "Beverly Hills, 90210," which ran for 10 seasons from 1990 to 2000. (FilmMagic)
The brief message comes as Spelling steps away from one of the projects that kept her closely connected to her "Beverly Hills, 90210" past.
Spelling recently confirmed she is no longer participating in "90210MG," the rewatch podcast she launched with former co-star Jennie Garth in 2020.
The "90210MG" podcast launched in November 2020, with Spelling and Garth revisiting "Beverly Hills, 90210" from the beginning and sharing memories from their years on the hit teen drama.
The rewatch has taken listeners back to West Beverly High, the Peach Pit and other memorable moments from the series while offering behind-the-scenes stories from the cast.

Nearly six years after its launch, the podcast is working its way through Season 8 of the show's 10-season run. Spelling's departure means she will not continue alongside Garth for the final stretch of the rewatch.
Spelling addressed her departure more directly during a recent episode of Brian Austin Green's "Hump Day Live," a weekly video series that streams on the Origami Network.
When Green suggested she needed "a little time" to gather her thoughts about the situation, Spelling agreed.

"I like the way you phrased that," she said. "Yeah. You want to really take the time, really assess, really reflect and then be able to speak your truth in a thoughtful way instead of a reactive way."
Green noted that he tries to avoid ruling anything out permanently, while Spelling did not directly say whether she could eventually return to the podcast.
Instead, she encouraged fans to continue supporting Garth and co-host Amy Sugarman.

Spelling encouraged fans to keep listening to the podcast despite her departure. (Harry Langdon/Getty Images)
"Please, please, please keep watching," Spelling said. "Jennie and Amy [Sugarman] are doing it. They’re bringing on tons of fun hosts, so please keep watching it."
The exchange also highlighted Spelling’s enduring friendship with Green, who played her on-screen love interest, David Silver, opposite her Donna Martin on "Beverly Hills, 90210."
The two recently reunited for what Spelling called a "play date," sharing photos together on Instagram and prompting nostalgic reactions from fans.
"David and Donna together again.💕 so awesome that you two have remained friends all these years," one commenter wrote.
Green said he lacked "self-confidence" during the nearly two-decade-long rift with Spelling. (Getty Images)
Spelling has also been openly affectionate about her decades-long bond with Green.
For his birthday in July, she shared a tribute reflecting on how their friendship has evolved since their days working together on the hit series.
"He’s a little bit VINYL… I’m a little bit THREAD 🎵💃🏼. Happy Birthday @brianaustingreen," Spelling wrote.

"What a dream it’s been to grow with you. I’d choose you every lifetime. I love you with every ounce of my being. Don’t ever stop pushing me to be the best version of myself and I promise to never stop making you laugh! xo"

Spelling and Green's bond stretches back to their teenage years on "Beverly Hills, 90210," where they spent a decade playing fan-favorite couple Donna and David. Their relationship wasn't limited to the screen. The co-stars became romantically involved early in the show's run.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Spelling and Green have since reconnected and are close friends. (FOX Image Collection via Getty Images)

Their lives eventually moved in different directions, and the two went years without communicating after the series ended. They have since found their way back to a close friendship, with Green now among the people Spelling has turned to while navigating changes in her personal and professional life.
Spelling’s decision to leave "90210MG" came with two seasons remaining in the podcast’s effort to rewatch all 10 seasons of the original series.
Garth addressed Spelling’s departure during the July 31 episode of "90210MG," admitting she was disappointed they wouldn't complete the rewatch together.
"I’m sad that she’s not finishing this out with us. We started this together. I’m sad about that, if I’m honest," Garth said.
However, she also expressed support for her former co-star’s decision.
TORI SPELLING SETS THE RECORD STRAIGHT ON 30 YEARS OF PLASTIC SURGERY RUMORS
Spelling has remained connected to the hit series decades after its debut. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Lionsgate;Steve Starr/CORBIS/Corbis via Getty Images)
"I’m really happy for her," Garth said. "I’m excited for her to choose herself."
Sugarman said Spelling’s departure was her own decision.
"This was 100% her decision," she said.
She added that the team could be disappointed by Spelling’s departure while still supporting whatever comes next.

"We can be really bummed, disappointed that she’s not going to do seasons 9 and 10 with us, with you, while still wanting her to be happy and to be excited for her about the things she is working on and does want to do," Sugarman said.

title: Antonio Banderas says he always knew Los Angeles wasn't where he belonged

story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Antonio Banderas is getting real about why he ditched Los Angeles to move back to his hometown in Spain.

During a recent interview with People, the 65-year-old explained he originally moved to Los Angeles to be with Melanie Griffith after the two fell in love. She had two young children at the time and couldn't relocate to Spain.

"Those were beautiful, exciting years. But I always had this sense of provisionality that it was not going to last my whole life," Banderas said. "I knew that Málaga was there, my hometown. I was not supposed to be in Malibu, but in Málaga."

Griffith and Banderas got married in 1996, just one year after making a connection on set of the 1995 movie "Two Much." Not long after tying the knot, the two welcomed their daughter, Stella, in September 1996.
Banderas always knew he would return to his hometown in Spain after moving to Los Angeles to be with Melanie Griffith. (Carlos Alvarez/Getty Images)
'FIRE COUNTRY' STAR DIANE FARR LEAVES LOS ANGELES AFTER 30 YEARS TO START HER 'THIRD ACT'
The two were married for 18 years before Griffith filed for divorce in June 2014, citing irreconcilable differences. They finalized their divorce a little over a year later in December 2015.
"When we separated, we were always very sincere. And now she is, if not my best friend, one of my best friends," Banderas explained.
While married to Griffith, Banderas was stepfather to her two children, Alexander Bauer and actress Dakota Johnson.
When speaking to E! News in February 2025, Banderas admitted he "would love to work with Dakota someday," not only because she is his family, but "because she's a good actress."

title: Jamie Kennedy blasts left-wing double standards after 'maggot' attacks
summary: Jamie Kennedy says he's labeled a "maggot" for supporting Trump policies and slams the left as fake on inclusion during a fiery podcast episode.
story: Comedian Jamie Kennedy spoke to Fox News Digital about the state of comedy amid a highly polarized political landscape.
Jamie Kennedy is calling out what he sees as hypocrisy in America today.

The actor released a solo episode of his podcast, "Hate to Break It to Ya," this week and spoke at length about current events, namely the Fauci hearings and the renewed conversation about the COVID-19 pandemic and its lasting effects.
During the episode, Kennedy's discussion of the public response to the pandemic became a bit broader when he spoke about some people today being "beyond brainwashed."
JAMIE KENNEDY BLASTS MARK HAMILL'S DEAD TRUMP POST AS 'EVIL' AFTER ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT
Jamie Kennedy says people have called him a "maggot" because of his political beliefs. (Barry Brecheisen/WireImage)

"And I've never seen this in the history of our race of human beings," he continued. "For instance, if I like something that a Republican does, or Trump does, they call me not just MAGA, they call me a maggot. A maggot."

He explained that while he does lean right, he "never even voted," and he said there are some more liberal policies he agrees with, "but if I say I like that Trump secures the borders, I'm just a maggot."
The "Scream" star said he believes that people like him, who focus on policy over party, are "open-minded," while people on the left have "no leniency."

"How can you say that you're the party of inclusion when you don't include us?" he asked. "All we want to do is talk to people, figure out things, go through different ideas, see what we like. And if we don't, we don't feel like we've looked under every stone. And I feel like that's what's happening. People don't want you to investigate. If you even investigate or go against their beliefs, they just put you in a box."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Kennedy says he believes people like him are "open-minded." (Gabe Ginsberg/Getty Images)

Kennedy also spoke about performing an hour-long comedy set in a parking lot to raise money for a bar that had been struggling to stay afloat under lockdown restrictions. The event was nearly shut down while, at the same time, he claimed, a crew of dozens was shooting a television show in another parking lot nearby with no issues because it had been "sanctioned by the state."
"That's the hypocrisy," he complained. "A female, family-owned business, probably very left-leaning ... and you've turned them into me. And you know what you think I am.

"So, when you say that people are like this, it's because you're so repressive. You're so judgmental, you're so mean. You're so arrogant, you're so impatient, you're so ... there's nothing sweet about you. There's nothing open or forgiving."
Kennedy spoke about what he sees as the differences between the right and the left on his podcast. (Frazer Harrison/Getty Images)

title: 'Remember the Titans' star Ethan Suplee says one hard truth fueled his 300-pound weight loss
summary: Ethan Suplee reveals how treating weight loss like his sobriety helped him maintain a 300-pound transformation after years of failed attempts.
story: Ethan Suplee reflects on the ongoing responsibility that comes with becoming a public weight loss success story and explains why consistent support from like-minded people keeps him on track.

"Remember the Titans" star Ethan Suplee spent years dramatically transforming his body, but the actor says the breakthrough that finally helped him maintain his weight loss came when he stopped viewing it as something he could permanently "cure."

Suplee explained he saw the biggest change when he began treating his relationship with food and weight much like his sobriety, a lifelong condition requiring honesty, communication and accountability.

Reflecting on his recovery journey with Fox News Digital, Suplee said repeated attempts to get sober failed because he believed he could simply complete rehab and move on. He believed taking 30 days away from drugs and alcohol meant the problem had gone away.
"I haven’t had drugs or alcohol in 30 days," he recalled. "That means I’m cured."
'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE ISSUES WARNING ABOUT WEIGHT LOSS DRUG CRAZE
Ethan Suplee revealed his weight loss journey changed when he stopped searching for a "cure" and treated it like his sobriety. (Getty Images)
It wasn't until he embraced ongoing accountability and open communication that he found lasting success, a lesson he later realized applied just as much to maintaining his weight loss.
"My condition isn’t a condition with a cure," Suplee explained. "It’s a condition that I can learn to manage.

"I did not apply that to weight loss for many, many years. I kind of was doing everything in my head, and the big boon to actually being able to maintain it was finding a group of people to be accountable to."
WATCH: ‘REMEMBER THE TITANS’ STAR REVEALS THE KEY TO HIS LASTING WEIGHT LOSS
CELEBRITY CHEF REVEALS NO. 1 MISTAKE SABOTAGING YOUR WEIGHT LOSS: 'FUZZY MATH'
Ethan Suplee shed 300 pounds through lifestyle changes. (Courtesy of Ethan Suplee)

Suplee has been candid about his decades-long battle with obesity. The "My Name is Earl" actor weighed roughly 500 pounds at his heaviest and ultimately lost around 300 pounds through years of diet and lifestyle changes. He has also undergone multiple skin-removal surgeries and now hosts weekly discussions on his show, "LifeLong with Ethan Suplee," about long-term weight management.
"There’s some pressure from the world to continue to manage [the weight loss]," he told Fox News Digital. "But that’s something I’ve kind of designed."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Ethan Suplee gained fame in "My Name is Earl" and "Remember the Titans." (Hopper Stone/NBC/NBCU Photo Bank)

On his weekly live show and podcast, Suplee regularly discusses the realities of long-term weight maintenance, inviting experts and people who have transformed their health to talk about nutrition, emotional eating, fitness and accountability. The show's central message is that health is an ongoing practice — not a destination.
"It’s a group of people, like-minded people, who come in, and we share what we’re going through, and we share our experience," Suplee explained. "And I think we all do better because of that."

After decades of trial and error, Suplee said his own experience taught him there is no shortcut to lasting weight loss. While he acknowledged that weight loss drugs can be an effective tool, he argued they aren't a replacement for building healthier habits.

"As a kid, I wanted a magical diet drug so badly. And now we have what is a magical diet drug," he said. "I think, unfortunately, it's also not a one-stop shop. I think you can hop on a GLP-1 and experience weight loss. You can see the scale go down week over week for a long time without having to do anything else.
"I think when people imagine their ideal, I don't think the GLP-1s get anyone to their ideal."
WATCH: ‘REMEMBER THE TITANS’ STAR ETHAN SUPLEE WARNS POPULAR GLP-1 DRUGS AREN'T A CURE-ALL FOR LASTING WEIGHT LOSS
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Suplee said his own experience shaped a simple philosophy: There's no single answer when it comes to long-term weight loss.
He emphasized that lasting success comes from addressing the many factors that influence a person's health and relationship with food.

"I don't think it's ever going to be one thing," Suplee explained. "I think it is partially the amount of food you're consuming, partially the types of food you're consuming, partially how sedentary you are and partially your emotional and potentially mental behavior and relationship with food."

title: Carmen Electra says 'Baywatch' pushed boundaries without crossing the line: 'It wasn't porn'
summary: Carmen Electra reveals what made the original "Baywatch" a global phenomenon while promoting the new competition show, "Nation's Dumbest," on Fox.
story: Carmen Electra shares her thoughts on what it takes to keep the ‘spark alive’ in relationships.
Carmen Electra is reminiscing about her days starring in the original "Baywatch."
In a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old "Nation's Dumbest" contestant discussed the success of the original series, saying all "the cast members made it special."
"It's hard to replace Pamela [Anderson] and Yasmine [Bleeth] and all those people. And there was just a certain tone. I don't know how to explain it," she said.

"It had a certain tone to it that it was just such a fantasy, and maybe it was the first time on television you could see so much skin because we really were playing lifeguards, right? So, we could be in these skimpy outfits."
BROOKS NADER SIZZLES IN ICONIC RED SWIMSUIT AS SHE SHARES BEHIND THE SCENES SNAPS FROM 'BAYWATCH' REBOOT SET
She said the show possibly left people thinking, "Oh my God, what is this? We can see nipples."
Electra credits the success of "Baywatch" to the sexy nature of the show. (Gerome Defrance/Getty Images)

"And it wasn't porn. You know, what I mean? They didn't have to sneak away and find a VHS tape to, like, sneak and put in. You can watch this," she added. "You can also learn something. Because we heard from a lot of people, a lot of fans out there, that they learned so much watching the show."

Electra cited the show's sexy nature as one of the reasons it became the global phenomenon it is, saying they were "sometimes trying to be sexy, sometimes not trying to be sexy" and, "all of a sudden, you get these guys on there with these gorgeous bodies."

In addition to the sexy aspect of the show, Electra attributed its success to the fact that fans could learn something from the show, including how to give CPR, adding she also "learned how to give CPR."
"I could save someone right now if I needed to," she joked.
The actress and model joined the show in 1997 for its eighth season after gaining exposure from posing for Playboy in a 1996 pictorial.
Electra joined the show in the eighth season. (Gerome Defrance/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

In terms of returning for the new reboot of the series, Electra is open to putting on the iconic red one-piece once again, since her former love interest on the show, David Chokachi has signed on to return.

"I could do something. Come in, have another love scene with David Chokachi. Just something really cute and fun. I would be down to get into the water again," she said. "I think it would be fun. It makes sense. I was David Chokachi's love interest way back then. I think it would be really fun and why not, you know?"
His character, Cody Madison, is now the owner of a beachside bar, The Shoreline, and acts as a mentor to the younger new lifeguards.
"I think it would be so cool if I just came in for an episode to surprise him and say hi. They fall in love again, who knows?" Electra said.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Electra said she is willing to make an appearance on the "Baywatch" reboot. (Getty Images)
One thing the actress is not willing to go through again is "the schooling that I did when I first joined the cast.
"That was really tough," she noted.
After her time on "Baywatch," Electra had a successful career in both film and television, appearing in films such as "Scary Movie," "Cheaper by the Dozen 2," "Meet the Spartans" and others.

She also recently appeared as a contestant on "Nation's Dumbest," a new celebrity competition show. She told Fox News Digital she originally didn't want to do it, saying, "I didn't pay attention in school" and that she "didn't have a good feeling about it."

"Fox kept getting on the phone. They're like, it's gonna be so easy. It's gonna be fun. It's like acting. Think of it as an acting role," she said. "Once I was not there anymore, I kind of missed it ... and there was a lot of fun. I did miss the cast a lot, but, yeah, I think we were all sitting there going, 'What? Why the hell did we subject ourselves to be on this show?'
Electra and Hilaria Baldwin competing in a challenge for "Nation's Dumbest." (Shane Mahood/ FOX)

"I definitely had a lot of anxiety, and I would freeze. As soon as we would have to rush and say something, answer a question really fast or there was something weird we had to do," she added. "It could be very stressful and I would freeze."

When it came to a moment that still haunts her, Electra couldn't believe she couldn't remember what BBL stood for, saying the producers threw in "a really easy question that she's gonna get and I got it wrong. I couldn't believe it."

The show features celebrity contestants who take on pop quizzes and physical challenges with the goal of being eliminated as early as possible to avoid being the last one standing and being named the nation's dumbest.
Electra was eliminated after the fourth episode of the show, which aired Aug. 5.
Electra was eliminated from the show in its fourth episode. (Shane Mahood/FOX)
"Nation's Dumbest" airs Wednesdays at 9 p.m. on Fox, with new episodes available the following day on Hulu.

title: 'Seinfeld' star Patrick Warburton says making out with Carol Burnett felt 'like kissing mom'
summary: Patrick Warburton recalls making out with Carol Burnett at age 27, plus his unexpected encounters with Betty White and Bea Arthur over the years.
story: During an appearance on 'Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia,' the ‘Seinfeld’ star recalls filming romantic scenes with Carol Burnett, revealing the actress's playful joke. He also reflects on other unforgettable TV legends.
Before Patrick Warburton became a fan favorite as David Puddy on "Seinfeld," he found himself in an unlikely role: Carol Burnett's much younger lover.
On "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia," the actor recalled what it was like being paired with the legendary comedian in a skit.

"I made out with her," he told Sibilia. "I was 27 at the time, and she played a soap star. She played the good sister, the good twin and the evil twin. They were both dating the same toy boy, which was 27-year-old me."
At the time, Burnett was in her late 50s.
CAROL BURNETT REVEALS WHAT SHE MISSES ABOUT COMEDY: ‘I DON’T THINK A NETWORK WOULD TAKE A CHANCE’

In an Aug. 2, 2026, episode of "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia," Patrick Warburton, left, spoke about locking lips with legendary comedienne Carol Burnett, right. (Scott Gries/ImageDirect; Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
"I’d have scenes where I was making out with the good one and the bad one, [and they] were both Carol," he explained.
"Carol was adorable. When we’re doing that, she looks to the director and goes, ‘Oh, we’re going to have to rehearse this some more.’ That was very cute and very sweet.

"For me, it was kind of like kissing mom because I grew up with the family on ‘The Carol Burnett Show,’" he continued. "But it is funny as I look back. I made out with Carol Burnett. ... Me and the older gals, I don’t know."
WATCH: PATRICK WARBURTON RECALLS KISSING CAROL BURNETT AT AGE 27
The 61-year-old joked there appeared to be a trend.
"I had a 94-year-old Betty White rub my naked chest down in bed in a show," Warburton told the outlet. "I have very interesting Eartha Kitt stories. Nothing too lascivious, but it’s just odd."
Another "Golden Girls" legend kept Warburton on his toes.
Betty White and Patrick Warburton in an episode of "The Fixer." (Vivian Zink/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images via Getty Images)

"I remember Bea Arthur was doing a three-episode arc on a TV show I was doing, and I was about 27 at the time when I did that as well," he explained. "There were about seven or eight of us that were all supposed to go get sushi for lunch. Everybody backed out. Bea Arthur looks at me, and she goes, ‘I want sushi, don’t you?’ And I go, ‘Well, yeah, I wanted it.’ And she goes, ‘You and I will go.’

"So, now I'm having lunch with Bea Arthur, and I'm 27," he continued. "Bea was lovely, but as we all know, Bea was also — there was just something kind of scary and imposing about that woman. And the character she played was not one to be trifled with.

"And I just felt very uncomfortable just sitting there at first having lunch with Bea. [But] we had a lovely lunch. She mostly talked about rescuing greyhound dogs because that was her cause. It's just weird, Joe. Me and the older gals, I don't know."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Patrick Warburton as David Puddy and Julia Louis-Dreyfus as Elaine Benes in "The Burning" episode of "Seinfeld." (Joey Delvalle/NBCU Photo Bank)
Warburton later became a fan favorite as Puddy on the '90s sitcom "Seinfeld" and has voiced paraplegic police officer Joe Swanson on Seth MacFarlane's "Family Guy" since 1999.
Warburton previously spoke to Fox News Digital about how his parents, John and Barbara Warburton, had a particularly strong dislike of "Family Guy."
Actor Patrick Warburton attends the "Family Guy" mobile game launch party at the Happy Ending Bar in Hollywood April 2, 2014. (Tommaso Boddi/WireImage)

"They don't see it as satire. They see it as blasphemy," Warburton said. "So, it was just a conversation that we were never really able to have. We never saw eye to eye on it. But, yeah, they always hated that show."
WATCH: PATRICK WARBURTON DISCUSSES RELIGIOUS BACKGROUND AND FINDING OUT SECRET HERITAGE

Warburton said his parents objected to the animated series on moral grounds because they were "very religious." John, who died in 2018, spent three months at the Abbey of Our Lady of Gethsemani in Bardstown, Kentucky, where Thomas Merton was his spiritual advisor. He nearly became a monk before deciding to pursue a career in medicine.
According to Warburton, Barbara shared her husband's devout Catholic faith and his strong disapproval of their son's most popular shows.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Patrick Warburton attends An Un-fur-gettable Night with "Zootopia 2" Feb. 25, 2026, in Los Angeles. (Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
"If Mom could possibly be worse than Dad, she is, yes," Warburton joked.
Warburton recalled that his mother's religious convictions led to another attempt to influence his work.

"I remember back in the day when we lived in Woodland Hills, my mom and dad came to visit. And we were in the kitchen, and my mom says, 'Are you going to work on "Seinfeld" today?' And I said, 'I am, as a matter of fact.' And she said, ‘I have this dynamic videotape that has converted a lot of my Jewish friends. If I gave it to you, would you give it to Jerry?’" Warburton recalled with a laugh.

John O'Hurley as J. Peterman, Keith Hernandez as himself and Patrick Warburton as David Puddy appear in "The Finale: Part 1&2," episodes 23 and 24 of "Seinfeld." (Joseph Del Valle/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
Warburton said his mother didn't easily give up on her goal of converting Jerry Seinfeld to Catholicism.

"Years later, Jerry was performing [stand-up] in Pensacola, Florida," Warburton said. "And mom and dad wanted to go. And I go, 'I'll hook you up.' So, I call up Jerry, get them a couple of tickets. So, I talked to my mom after the show, and I go, ‘Did you enjoy Jerry?' And she goes, ’He was wonderful. I even wrote him a lovely thank-you letter.'

"And, at that point, that's when the hair on the back of my neck stood up, and I go, 'You probably didn't just leave a letter, did you, Mom? You probably left a DVD.' And she goes, ‘I did,'" Warburton continued. "I go, ‘Do you know how disrespectful that is?’ And she said, ‘I only answer to one person, the Lord above.’ So, that's how they operate. That's how Mom operates."
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Actor Patrick Warburton participates in the "Acting in Independent Film" panel discussion at the South by Southwest Film Festival in Austin March 12, 2000. (John Anderson/Getty Images)
Warburton told Fox News Digital he later brought up his mother's unexpected gift when he ran into Seinfeld in New York.
"We had a laugh, but yeah, I'm sure he didn't watch it," he said.
"He hasn't converted yet, as far as I know."
Patrick Warburton visits the AOL Build Speaker Series to discuss his NBC comedy "Crowded" at AOL Studios in New York March 15, 2016. (Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images)
Though Warburton has previously described himself as a "bad Catholic," he told Fox News Digital he has "absolutely" had moments when he felt uncomfortable with some of his work because of his faith.
"Catholic guilt runs deep," he acknowledged. "But I believe God has a sense of humor."
Fox News Digital's Ashley Hume contributed to this report.
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Morgan Fairchild says two men once abducted her off NYC street as bystanders laughed
summary: Morgan Fairchild revealed on her new podcast how she joked her way to freedom in 1970 after being abducted off a New York City street while visiting her sister.
story: Lorenzo Lamas told Fox News Digital he handles Hollywood stress by riding his Harley along the coast and reconnecting with nature.
Morgan Fairchild believes her sense of humor may have saved her life.

The actress, whose role on "Flamingo Road" cemented her bombshell image before she became a glamorous vixen on "Falcon Crest," has a new podcast, "2 B----es From Texas," co-hosted with her sister, Cathryn Hartt.
The show features never-before-heard stories from their decades in showbiz and sit-down interviews with celebrity friends.
On a recent episode, Fairchild recalled being abducted on a New York City street before fame came calling. While it was no laughing matter, Fairchild said she managed to joke her way to freedom.
MORGAN FAIRCHILD REFUSED TO ‘SELL MY SOUL’ FOR HOLLYWOOD FAME
Morgan Fairchild in 1984 promoting the TV special "Blondes vs Brunettes." She is now the co-host of the podcast "2 B----es From Texas." (Bob D'Amico /American Broadcasting Companies via Getty Images)
The 20-year-old Dallas native was visiting her sister in 1970 when the terrifying ordeal unfolded.
"I'm walking up at two o'clock in the afternoon, broad daylight, no reason to be scared," Fairchild recalled to Fox News Digital.
Morgan Fairchild and her sister Cathryn Hartt in New York City, circa 1982. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"And this one big guy comes up talking to me. Now, I'm from Texas, but I know you're not supposed to talk to people on the street in New York. You don't talk to gentlemen. So I'm just ignoring him. And then this other big guy comes up on the other side of me. And these guys are both over 6 feet tall. They just grabbed me up by the elbows and threw me in this cab that was loitering there that I hadn't noticed."
WATCH: LORENZO LAMAS SHARES HOW HE MANAGES THE PRESSURES OF FAME

Fairchild said several people were waiting at a nearby bus stop, while others were walking by. Realizing she was in danger, she screamed for help. Fairchild said they must have thought she was "a hooker or something."
"Nobody lifted a finger," she said. "In fact, some of them laughed. And that made me realize how easy it would be to totally disappear and nobody would ever know what happened to you.
Morgan Fairchild, left, and Barbara Eden attend Remus Pre Award Tea Time at The Beverly Hills Hotel March 8, 2023, in Beverly Hills. (Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images for Marcel Remus)

"The cab has very thick plexiglass between the passengers and the driver," Fairchild recalled. "I don't think the driver spoke much English. But these guys started telling me all the things they were going to do to me. That's how I found out that one was a pimp and the other was a pusher. The one who was a pusher was telling me all the things he was going to shoot me up with. And the pimp was telling me all the things that he was going to do to my body.
American actress Morgan Fairchild poses at a party hosted by Wilhelmina Cooper at the Excelsior Club in New York City on June 23, 1975. (Tim Boxer/Getty Images)
"I was a shy kid, but I was damned if I was going to let them see how scared I was," Fairchild added.
Fairchild said every time her abductors described what they were going to do to her, she responded with "a wisecrack."
Morgan Fairchild, right, made many pals in Hollywood over the years, including Loni Anderson. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"I had them laughing," Fairchild said. "At one point, unbelievably to me, one of them looked at the other and said, 'She's funny. Let's let her go.' And they did. They gave the cab driver some money and said, 'Take her wherever she wants to go.' Well, I went back to my sister's apartment.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Morgan Fairchild, left, and her sister Cathryn Hartt pose in New York City circa 1980. (Robin Platzer/IMAGES/Getty Images)
"I didn't come out for three days," she admitted. "Intro to New York 101. It was very, very scary."
Fairchild still wonders how she managed to think so quickly while fearing for her life.
Morgan Fairchild attends the Chiller Theatre Expo Spring 2019 at the Parsippany Hilton on April 26, 2019, in Parsippany, N.J. (Bobby Bank/Getty Images)

"I have no clue," she said. "It was all intuitive because I was not going to let them see how scared I was. That's what I did. I had to talk my way out of it by being funny, just being a wise a--. It's like an improvisation class.

"Somebody says something, and you come up with something else and make the scene work. It's like that, only much more dangerous. I've talked my way out of things a couple of times in my life just by being a wise a--.

After surviving a terrifying abduction in New York at just 20 years old, Morgan Fairchild went on to build an extraordinary career, becoming one of television’s most recognizable stars. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"My sister had been living in New York for a little bit," she said. "I was the naïve one from Texas. Although naïve doesn't really cover it because I wasn't doing anything stupid. I was just walking in broad daylight. It wasn't in a dark alley, coming out of a club drunk or any of those other things that could make you vulnerable."
Fairchild said she shared the story on her podcast to encourage women to be aware of their surroundings.
Morgan Fairchild urges women to be mindful of their surroundings. (Vinnie Zuffante/Getty Images)

"I think what women really need to keep in mind is how easy it is for you to just disappear," said Fairchild. "People were laughing at me as they were throwing me into this car. That, to me, was one of the scariest things: the lack of feeling for your fellow man. And you don’t think something like this could really ever happen to you."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Morgan Fairchild as Jordan Roberts on "Falcon Crest," circa 1985. (CBS via Getty Images)
The experience has stayed with Fairchild. To this day, she keeps watch on her surroundings.

"I always scan buildings," she said. "I keep an eye out all the time to see if I'm being followed. I do it surreptitiously, so people don't really realize, but I'm watching. I'm checking things in a rearview mirror. If I'm in a building, I check to see where the exits are. You have to be aware of your surroundings.
"I say this to women because they're always on their cellphones, and that makes them so vulnerable.
Morgan Fairchild attends the 2020 Hollywood Beauty Awards at The Taglyan Complex on Feb. 6, 2020, in Los Angeles. (Tibrina Hobson/Getty Images)

"They're not paying attention to what's going on around them. They're not paying attention to who's following them, whether somebody could be hiding around a corner. I'm now very aware all the time. I never walk and text. And that's what I tell women. Never walk and text. A lot of young women tend to make that mistake. When you walk and text, you become so unaware of anything around you that's happening. You're assuming that you're safe. Never assume that you're safe."
Beyond revisiting stories from her past, Fairchild said she hopes the podcast encourages listeners to show more kindness.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Morgan Fairchild attends the Farrah Fawcett Foundation 2025 Tex-Mex Fiesta at The Rustic on Oct. 30, 2025, in Dallas. (Omar Vega/Getty Images for Farrah Fawcett Foundation)

"It's been really fun getting to connect with friends again," Fairchild said. "And it's fun that our listeners are reacting to these stories. And you know, on my social media, I sign off with the hashtag #bekind. And I think that's one thing that's missing in our society these days: kindness and trying to understand other people's points of view."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Earth, Wind & Fire abruptly postpones show after band member’s medical emergency
summary: Earth, Wind & Fire canceled its Chase Center show with Lionel Richie due to a band member's medical emergency. A rescheduled date is pending.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

The legendary group announced the unexpected change shortly before its scheduled performance Thursday at the Chase Center.

"As a result, tonight’s show with Lionel Richie will be rescheduled, with a new date to be announced soon.

Earth, Wind & Fire abruptly canceled a concert Aug. 6 due to a medical emergency. The show with Lionel Richie will be rescheduled. (Medios y Media/Getty Images)

"Ticket holders should retain their tickets, which will be honored for the new date, or refunds will be available at the point of purchase," the statement continued. "We sincerely apologize for the unexpected change and appreciate everyone’s understanding."
No additional details about the nature of the medical emergency were immediately provided.

title: ‘Sopranos’ stars reunite in emotional farewell for Vincent Pastore
summary: Steven Van Zandt served as a pallbearer at Vincent Pastore's funeral, revealing he spoke to his "Sopranos" co-star just one day before his death.
story: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports on the death of ‘Sopranos' star Vincent Pastore at age 80 on ‘Fox Report.’
Years after "The Sopranos" came to an end, its stars reunited for a heartbreaking reason — to say goodbye to Vincent Pastore.

Pastore was laid to rest Thursday in New York, surrounded by family and friends. His "Sopranos" co-star, Steven Van Zandt, served as a pallbearer, helping carry the late actor to his final resting place. Pastore's casket was draped with an American flag in honor of his time serving in the Navy.
Pastore's daughter remembered the man best known for the role of Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero as "a giving person."
"He was a man who lived out his dreams … but he knew how lucky he was," she said during the emotional funeral, Page Six reported.
'THE SOPRANOS' ACTOR VINCENT PASTORE DEAD AT 80
Pallbearers, including Steven van Zandt, carry the casket of actor Vincent Pastore during his funeral at Holy Family Church in New Rochelle, N.Y., Aug. 6. (James Keivom)
"I think that’s why he tried to share as much of it with as many people as possible," she added. "Whether that was a big tip, always in cash, or by shaking hands with every cop on every corner."
Maureen Van Zandt attends Vincent Pastore's funeral Aug. 6. (T. Jackson/Backgrid)
Van Zandt told the outlet he kept in touch with Pastore "quite often" before his death.

"We just happened to call him two days ago. The day before he died, we luckily just happened to call him," he said, referring to him and wife Maureen. "He was one of a kind, and we’ll miss him very much."
Days after his death, the actor's "right-hand man," Stephen Villano, told the Post Pastore was nothing like the character he often portrayed on the screen.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Vincent Pastore, right, rose to fame as a key character in "The Sopranos." (Getty Images)
"He said, ‘I’m an actor. I play a character.’ So, people would think that this is the man, but that wasn’t the man," he said. "The man was generous, he was kind, he was caring," Villano said.
"He cared about his neighbors, he cared about charities, he cared about fundraisers."
Villano said Pastore supported veterans in the Bronx, U.S. troops and the police department.
"He supported St. Jude’s [Children’s Research Hospital], and he supported the NYPD," Villano added. "Widows, orphans, their Christmas parties … all the time, back the blue."
Mourners pay their respects to Vincent Pastore at his funeral Aug. 6, 2026. (T. Jackson/Backgrid)
Pastore died Aug. 1.
"Vinny passed away either yesterday or today at home in The Bronx," his manager, Robert Attermann, said.

"I had the privilege of representing Vinny for more than 30 years, long before 'The Sopranos' made him a household name," he added. "To the world, he will always be remembered as the unforgettable 'Big Pussy,' but to those of us who knew him, he was so much more."
Vincent Pastore is survived by his daughter Renee. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)

In addition to Pastore's role on "The Sopranos," the actor also appeared in "Blue Bloods," "Law & Order," "General Hospital," "Bull," "Pair of Kings," "Hawaii Five-0" and most recently lent his voice on an episode of "Yellowjackets."
He also appeared in a number of movies, including "Goodfellas," "A Bronx Tale," "Carlito's Way," "Gotti," "Once Upon a Time in Brooklyn," "Mickey Blue Eyes" and others.

"He loved being an actor," Attermann said. "He was passionate about his craft and was always encouraging, respectful and generous with young actors, taking the time to offer guidance and support whenever he could."

title: Martha Stewart questions Meghan Markle’s homemaking credentials with blunt career assessment
summary: Martha Stewart questioned Meghan Markle's transition from actress to princess to homemaking guru, saying the career path "doesn't sort of follow."
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Martha Stewart is not entirely convinced Meghan Markle’s path into the lifestyle world adds up.

The 85-year-old homemaking icon offered a pointed assessment of the Duchess of Sussex’s transition from actress to royal to television host while discussing Markle’s Netflix series, "With Love, Meghan."
When asked about Markle stepping into her space with a cooking and lifestyle show, Stewart questioned whether the career transition made sense.
MEGHAN MARKLE RETURNS TO BRITAIN WITH PRINCE ARCHIE AND PRINCESS LILIBET FOR FIRST TIME IN YEARS
Martha Stewart questioned Meghan Markle's transition into the lifestyle television space during a recent interview. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images;Jonathan Brady / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)

"If you’re an actress, it’s hard to then transition to a princess and then from a princess into a homemaking guru on a television show," Stewart told People. "It doesn’t sort of follow. So go from there."
Stewart also revealed that she recently crossed paths with Markle at a dinner party in California shortly after the duchess returned from a family trip to the United Kingdom.
"I had dinner with Meghan Markle the other night," she said. "We were both guests at a dinner party in California. And she had just gotten back from the palace."
Stewart said their interaction was brief.
"I didn’t talk to her really more than to say a couple words, but I know she was talking about it," she added.
Last month, Markle traveled to Britain with Prince Harry and their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, marking the family’s first visit to England in four years.
King Charles and Queen Camilla hosted the Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their children for a private family meeting at Highgrove House in July.

The Sussexes moved to California in 2020 after stepping back as senior working members of the royal family. Markle later returned to the entertainment industry while expanding into media, business and lifestyle ventures.
MEGHAN MARKLE AND NETFLIX END LIFESTYLE BRAND PARTNERSHIP AS CRITICS SAY THEY 'GOT MARKLED ENOUGH'
Meghan Markle and Prince Harry married in 2018. (Chris Jackson)
"With Love, Meghan" premiered on Netflix in March 2025 and featured Markle sharing cooking, gardening, hosting and entertaining ideas with celebrity guests.
The series launched alongside her lifestyle brand, As Ever, which has sold products including fruit spreads, honey, tea, wine, candles and chocolate.
Stewart’s latest remarks echo comments she made in July 2025, when she was asked by Yahoo Lifestyle about Markle’s attempt to establish herself as a lifestyle authority.
"Meghan, I don’t really know very well, and I hope she knows what she’s talking about," Stewart told the outlet.
The cookbook author emphasized that credibility and experience are essential when building a connection with an audience.
"Authenticity, to me, is everything, and to be authentic and knowledgeable about your subject matter is extremely important," she said.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Martha Stewart has built one of the world's most recognizable lifestyle brands. (Getty Images for Friends of Hudson River Park)
Stewart added that she did not object to other celebrities entering the lifestyle industry, offering a brief message to those following in her footsteps.
"I don’t mind. Good luck."
Stewart built her own homemaking empire after launching a catering business and publishing her first cookbook, "Entertaining," in 1982.

Her brand later expanded into magazines, television programs, books, retail partnerships and home products. She became the first self-made female billionaire in the United States in 1999.
The Netflix series ran for two seasons and was followed by a holiday special.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, relocated to California in 2020. (Karwai Tang)
In March 2026, Netflix and Markle announced they were ending their partnership involving As Ever, with the duchess continuing to operate the lifestyle brand independently.

"Meghan’s passion for elevating everyday moments in beautiful yet simple ways inspired the creation of the As Ever brand, and we are glad to have played a role in bringing that vision to life," a Netflix spokesperson told Fox News Digital at the time.

"As it was always intended, Meghan will continue growing the brand and take it into its next chapter independently, and we look forward to celebrating how she continues to bring joy to households around the world."
In its own statement to People, As Ever said it was "grateful for Netflix’s partnership through launch and our first year."
