title: Popular weight-loss drugs may help protect against a deadly disease, doctor says
summary: A breast cancer surgeon explains how GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy may lower cancer recurrence risk by reducing BMI, estrogen and inflammation.
story: Dr. Loren Rourke, a Texas-based board-certified breast cancer surgeon, author and speaker, confirmed research has suggested that glucagon-like peptide-1 medications may be associated with a lower risk of cancer recurrence.

GLP-1 medications have transformed diabetes and obesity treatment, but emerging research suggests their benefits could extend far beyond those purposes — potentially even aiding in cancer prevention and survival.

Dr. Loren Rourke, a Texas-based board-certified breast cancer surgeon, author and speaker, said growing research suggests glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) medications — including Ozempic and Wegovy — may be associated with a lower risk of cancer diagnoses and recurrence.

She pointed to findings presented at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting in Chicago, where researchers reported an association between GLP-1 use and lower breast cancer recurrence rates, as well as a potential role in preventing the disease.
MILLIONS COULD GAIN EASIER ACCESS TO POPULAR PEPTIDES AFTER FDA PANEL VOTE
However, she noted that the evidence remains observational and can’t prove that the drugs reduce cancer risk.
Emerging research suggests that GLP-1 medications could aid in cancer prevention and survival. (iStock)

"So these aren’t studies that, unfortunately, patients can latch onto, call their doctor and say, ‘I want to get on a GLP-1 right now to reduce my risk of breast cancer or make my breast cancer better,’" Rourke told Fox News Digital. "However, what it did do was shine the light on GLP-1s and that relationship."
The cancer connection
The main reason that GLP-1s may aid in cancer prevention, according to Rourke, is that the drugs promote weight loss and reduce chronic inflammation.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"GLP-1s cause a decrease in your BMI. They cause weight reduction," she told Fox News Digital. "We know that a lower BMI equals a better prognosis with breast cancer."
In particular, post-menopausal women who are struggling with weight gain could get an extra benefit, the doctor said. (iStock)
"So if the secondary effect of taking a GLP-1 means you’re going to lose weight, then that’s a benefit, because we know you’re going to do better with breast cancer."
Diabetes and obesity medications can also lower estrogen production associated with excess body fat, the surgeon noted.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"The more fat you have, the higher your estrogen production," Rourke said. "You’re kind of bathing your body in estrogen, so to speak. So it intuitively makes sense that we are seeing this correlation or association."
GLP-1s also decrease the inflammatory state in which cancer thrives, the surgeon noted.
"The more fat we have, the higher your estrogen production."
"So if it’s fixing the overall chronic inflammation of the body, that’s going to help for a lot of reasons," she said.
"I think this is going to extend beyond breast cancer, but we need to get that scientific proof of a direct cause — is this just an association or a correlation?"
More research needed
Rourke emphasized that researchers have not yet proven that GLP-1 medications directly affect breast cancer cells.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"But this study has now garnered enough attention, interest and scientific hypotheses that the work is getting started for the randomized controlled trials that we’re all waiting for — and then we can act upon those."
The main reason that GLP-1s may aid in cancer prevention is that the drugs promote weight loss and reduce chronic inflammation, according to a doctor. (iStock)
To patients who are considering starting GLP-1s, Rourke offered the following advice.

"My bottom-line message on this one is, if you have an elevated BMI, you’re trying to lose weight, you’ve tried a healthy diet, you’ve tried to exercise, and you’re not winning that fight, consider GLP-1s, and you’re going to get a secondary benefit."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
In particular, post-menopausal women who are struggling with weight gain could get an extra benefit, Rourke added, but she urges them to "call their doctor and have that one-on-one conversation."

title: Bernie Sanders demands Democrats ban super PACs from primaries, blasts AIPAC, ‘corrupt system’
summary: Sanders is urging Democratic leaders to ban super PACs from party primaries, citing concerns about outside spending and influence.
story: Michigan GOP U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers argues Democrats have harmed Michigan's economy, leading to job losses and higher living cost, on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’
Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., is urging Democratic leaders to restrict super PAC involvement in party primaries, arguing that wealthy outside groups have too much influence over Democratic nominations.
In a post on X on Sunday, Sanders singled out the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC, while criticizing outside spending in Democratic primaries.

"It is insane that the Democrats allow super PACs like AIPAC to spend millions in their primaries — only for those same special interests to help elect Republicans in the general election," Sanders wrote. "My message to Democratic leaders: Ban super PACs from Democratic primaries NOW."

Sanders also shared an Aug. 8 letter addressed to Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Democratic National Committee Chairman Ken Martin.
SANDERS' ANSWER WHEN ASKED IF HE WILL ENDORSE SOCIALIST HONG IN WISCONSIN SPARKS INSTANT MOCKERY: 'SAYS A LOT'

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on May 20, 2026. Sanders is calling on Democratic leaders to ban super PACs from participating in party primaries. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

In the letter, Sanders said AIPAC and affiliated groups spent more than $30 million in Michigan’s Democratic primary in an effort to defeat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed. He also said the group plans to spend tens of millions more to support Republican Mike Rogers in the general election.

"AIPAC is not the only super PAC or outside organization playing this role. Corporate super PACs — including crypto, AI and online betting special interests — have already spent a record $517 million this election cycle, shattering the record set in 2024," Sanders wrote.

His criticism focused not only on the amount of outside spending, but also on groups that he said try to influence Democratic primaries and then support Republican candidates if their preferred Democrat loses.

"What is particularly obscene is not only the outrageous amount of money coming into Democratic primaries from billionaire-funded super PACs, but the reality that these special interests have no particular desire to see Democrats win," he said.
BERNIE SANDERS TELLS JAMES CARVILLE TO START HIS OWN PARTY AS MODERATE DEMS WARN AGAINST 'EMBRACING EXTREMISM'

A visitor holds an AIPAC folder inside the Rayburn House Office Building on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., on March 12, 2024. In a Sunday post on X, Sanders took particular aim at the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

"It is absurd that they spend tens of millions of dollars to try to determine who the Democratic nominee is and, if they fail, then proceed to support the Republican candidate in the general election."
AIPAC says it supports pro-Israel candidates from both parties, according to its website.

"AIPAC is a grassroots membership organization with a PAC that supports pro-Israel Democratic and Republican candidates for Congress," as noted on its website. "The AIPAC PAC is funded by individual American citizens who care deeply about helping elect leaders who want to strengthen the partnership between the United States and Israel."
AIPAC is affiliated with United Democracy Project, a super PAC that says it works to help defeat "detractors — both Republicans and Democrats — of the U.S.-Israel relationship," its website states.
Sanders again called for a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United and for public financing of elections.

"Right now, the Democratic Party has the power to prohibit super PACs from participating in its primaries. That can be done. That must be done," Sanders wrote. "I urge you to take action and make clear that the Democratic Party will no longer maintain this corrupt system."
BERNIE SANDERS BLASTS FETTERMAN AS 'WAY OUT OF TOUCH' WITH AMERICANS AFTER GRAHAM PLATNER REBUKE

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., arrives for a news conference outside the U.S. Capitol on March 5, 2026. Sanders sent Schumer an Aug. 8 letter urging Democratic leaders to ban super PACs from party primaries. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Sanders added, "While there are ideological differences of opinion within the big tent of the party, I would hope that we can all agree that Republican special interests should not play a role in determining the outcome of Democratic primaries. The time to act is now."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
In May, Sanders and Rep. Summer Lee, D-Pa., introduced the Abolish Super PACs Act, which would cap individual contributions to super PACs at $5,000 and effectively eliminate them.
AIPAC, Sanders, Schumer, Martin, Jeffries and Rogers could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.
