title: Dad sues after school allegedly won't say if biological males can use daughter's bathroom
summary: A North Carolina father sued Cabarrus County Schools after officials allegedly refused to say whether biological males can use his daughter's bathroom.
story: America First Legal Foundation senior counsel Nicholas Barry shared more on the group's newest federal lawsuit over what North Carolina schools must tell parents in an interview with Fox News Digital.

EXCLUSIVE: A North Carolina father is suing his children's school district after he says officials would not answer whether biological males could be permitted to use the same restrooms as his fourth-grade daughter.

Brandon Matthews, whose daughter attends Mount Pleasant Elementary School, and whose son is entering his senior year at Mount Pleasant High School, asked both principals in May to notify him if a member of the opposite biological sex was permitted to use bathrooms or locker rooms used by his children.
Matthews did not ask officials to identify any student, according to his federal lawsuit.
But Matthews still doesn't know the answer, his attorney says.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS

A federal lawsuit against Cabarrus County Schools seeks disclosure of policies and practices governing access to sex-separated restrooms and locker rooms at two North Carolina schools. (Sara D. Davis/Getty Images, File)
"Brandon Matthews does not currently know whether a male is using his fourth grade daughter's bathroom," Nicholas Barry, senior counsel at America First Legal Foundation, told Fox News Digital.

"And does he have a constitutional right to know that? We say 'yes,'" Barry said. "Without that information, he's just in the dark and... He really can't make any good decisions without that information."
Matthews' concerns over the district's bathroom practices predate the lawsuit.
At a May 11 school board meeting, Matthews appeared with his daughter and urged officials to keep boys and girls in separate bathrooms.
"Nobody's targeting a child," Matthews told the board. "All we're asking is that the bathrooms are accessible to each gender. If they want that, then create a new bathroom."
LOUDOUN COUNTY HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT ACCUSED OF FILMING STUDENTS IN BATHROOM UNDER INVESTIGATION
WATCH: NORTH CAROLINA DAD CONFRONTS SCHOOL ON BATHROOM ACCESS:
Matthews then turned to his daughter and asked her to address the board.
"I'm personally a girl and I wouldn't want a boy following me in the girls' bathroom," she said. "It's inappropriate."

Matthews also used heated language during his remarks. He repeatedly warned officials that he could "get aggressive" and, while discussing protecting his daughter, said, "Anytime somebody touches this little girl, I'm gonna hang them from my garage."
Less than three weeks later, Matthews put his concerns in writing.

He asked his daughter's principal to notify him "in the event that any biological male is permitted to use the female restroom facilities" she uses. He made a similar request concerning his son's facilities.
CHRISTIAN COUNSELORS CHALLENGE WISCONSIN CONVERSION THERAPY BAN AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING

Brandon Matthews, the father of two Cabarrus County Schools students, is asking a federal judge to require the district to disclose its policies governing access to sex-separated facilities. (TNS/Getty Images, File)
Both principals responded June 8, according to court filings.

The elementary school principal said that "[b]ecause matters involving individual students are confidential," the school "cannot confirm, disclose, or provide advance notice regarding the status, identity, or accommodations of any particular student."

The principal told Matthews that if he or his daughter became aware of a specific situation affecting her experience, they could contact the school to discuss his concerns. The high school principal sent a nearly identical response, according to the filing.
Barry argues that didn't answer Matthews' question.
"The explanation is fairly straightforward. They don't want to answer him," Barry told Fox News Digital. "Well, nobody asked for individual student information, so that's a non-answer," he added.
VIRGINIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER ALLEGED POLICY OF KEEPING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS HIDDEN FROM PARENTS

Brandon Matthews says he remains unable to determine whether his children could be expected to share school restrooms or locker rooms with members of the opposite sex, according to court filings. (Houston Chronicle via Getty Images, File)

Matthews filed suit in the Middle District of North Carolina against the Cabarrus County Board of Education, Superintendent Dr. John Kopicki and the principals of his children's schools. America First Legal Foundation and co-counsel Philip Thomas are representing him.

On Friday, Matthews also sought a preliminary injunction asking the court to require the district to disclose its policies governing sex-separated bathrooms and locker rooms and whether members of the opposite sex are permitted to access, or have accessed, facilities used by his children.

Matthews, a practicing Christian, says in his sworn declaration that his religious beliefs include that sex is immutable and that his children should not be expected to undress or use restrooms in the presence of members of the opposite sex.
The lawsuit does not allege that Matthews knows a biological male has used his daughter's bathroom. His attorneys argue that he cannot determine whether it has happened or is permitted to happen.

Matthews said in a sworn declaration that he has been unable to locate a written, publicly available policy explaining when students at either of his children's schools may be expected to share restrooms or changing facilities with members of the opposite sex.
TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS WOKE SCHOOLS ACCUSED OF HIDING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS
Matthews sought a preliminary injunction asking the court to require the district to disclose its policies governing sex-separated bathrooms. (Getty Images, File)

At an April 13 school board meeting, School Board attorney William Isenhour said "the district addresses the [bathroom and locker room] situation at each school on a case-by-case basis with the goal of addressing concerns of all students and their families," according to court filings.
Fox News Digital sent Cabarrus County Schools detailed questions about the allegations, the district's bathroom policies, whether parents receive advance notice and its response to the lawsuit.

Matthews says he ultimately seeks advance notice and a meaningful opportunity to opt his children out before they are expected or required to use intimate facilities in the presence of a member of the opposite sex. His preliminary-injunction motion asks the court, while the case proceeds, to require the district to disclose its policies and whether opposite-sex individuals are permitted to access, or have accessed, facilities used by his children.
It also seeks notice when a member of the opposite sex "has been authorized to enter, or is expected to enter" a facility used by their child.
Barry told Fox News Digital that a victory could have implications beyond Cabarrus County.

"Yes, I think if we continue to push Mahmood forward, and we start getting wins on it, schools around the country are going to have to start disclosing to parents what their policies are and providing parents the opportunity to opt out," Barry said.
SJSU VOLLEYBALL SCANDAL PROBE FINDS TEAM ALLEGEDLY RECRUITED MALE FOR ADVANTAGE WITHOUT TELLING FEMALE PLAYERS
Matthews' attorneys rely heavily on the Supreme Court's decision in Mahmoud v. Taylor. (iStock)
"I do think as Mahmoud percolates out and as cases like this get decided, it's going to require that school districts provide notice and an opportunity to opt out to parents on this specific issue."
That is Barry's interpretation of what a victory could require. The court has not yet ruled on Matthews' claims.

Matthews' attorneys rely heavily on the Supreme Court's decision in Mahmoud v. Taylor, which involved parents seeking notice and an opportunity to opt their children out of certain LGBT classroom instruction on religious grounds.
AFL argues that if parents are entitled to notice in that context, the same principle should apply to children sharing bathrooms, locker rooms or changing facilities with members of the opposite sex.
Matthews alleges the district violated his rights under the Free Exercise Clause of the First Amendment and the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
The case is America First Legal's second lawsuit against Cabarrus County Schools over sex-separated facilities.
Its first lawsuit alleges female students at Cox Mill High School were required to share girls' restrooms, locker rooms and changing spaces with a biological male.
Those allegations are separate from Matthews' case and do not establish that a biological male has used the restroom at his daughter's elementary school.
Barry drew the same distinction in his interview with Fox News Digital.
WASHINGTON MOTHER SAYS SHE FOUND ADULT MALE SHOWERING IN WOMEN'S LOCKER ROOM DURING CHILDREN'S SWIM MEET

"The first lawsuit we filed, there are allegations that a male is using our three client females' restroom and locker rooms and changing spaces," Barry said. "Which is different than what we're doing here. Here, it's a straightforward attack on Cabarrus County Schools policy to get information about it and to know whether it's impacting our clients' daughter and son at school right now."
Matthews' attorneys also stressed in their preliminary-injunction motion that he is seeking information and notice, not an order barring another student from a particular facility.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Plaintiff seeks only notice and information—he does not seek to prevent any student from using any facility," they wrote.
Cabarrus County Schools did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

title: Mountain getaway rocked by ‘latest chapter’ of deadly violence as officials avoid gang label in tourist town
summary: Asheville, North Carolina, police link the deadly Biltmore Avenue shooting to a direct retaliatory act tied to earlier gun violence in the city.
story: WARNING: Graphic content—State Rep. Tricia Cotham, R-N.C., criticizes soft-on-crime policies on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’

Police in Asheville, North Carolina, say a downtown shooting that killed two people and wounded seven was a direct retaliatory act, though they have declined to call the violence gang-related in the Blue Ridge tourist town.

The early morning gunfire erupted July 19 near Biltmore Avenue and Short Coxe Avenue, an area near downtown businesses and nightlife. The Asheville Police Department (APD) said officers responded to the scene at about 2:20 a.m. and found multiple people suffering from gunshot wounds.

Two people died at the scene despite life-saving efforts, while seven others were taken to Mission Hospital, authorities said. Detectives recovered numerous shell casings and identified what police described as a large crime scene.
GUNMAN CHARGED AFTER WOUNDING 9 IN TUCSON NIGHTLIFE SHOOTING BEFORE COP TAKES HIM DOWN
People walk through downtown Asheville, North Carolina. (Getty Images)

The department initially said evidence suggested the shooting may have been connected to an earlier gun violence incident. Days later, Interim Police Chief Jackie Stepp said investigators had determined it was "a direct retaliatory act" tied to a July 5 shooting at an apartment complex.

Stepp said the deadly episode was the "latest chapter" in an ongoing pattern of retaliatory violence across the city. One person was shot in the July 5 incident, she said, and investigators made an arrest in that case.
People walk through downtown Asheville, North Carolina. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)
But the chief declined to classify the violence as gang-related at a community briefing on July 24, when reporters pressed her about whether the people involved belonged to rival gangs or families.

"These are two groups of individuals," Stepp said at the briefing. She said the groups had ties because the people involved knew one another and had committed "ongoing retaliatory acts" against each other.
Interim Asheville Police Chief Jackie Stepp speaks during a community briefing about the downtown shooting that killed two people and wounded seven. (Asheville Police Department YouTube)

Stepp said police had identified several persons of interest in the Biltmore Avenue case but were still working to locate and interview them. Stepp later reportedly told ABC local station WLOS that gang activity exists in the city, though she maintained the recent shootings are "not traditional gang activity."

At the community briefing, the question whether the violence should be called gang-related resurfaced when a local pastor who identified himself as a gang-prevention facilitator told Mayor Esther Manheimer he had offered the city a prevention program since 2016.

title: Nancy Guthrie ransom notes may be fake as renowned profiler says case looks more like burglary gone wrong
summary: A forensic psychologist questions the legitimacy of ransom notes in the Nancy Guthrie case but says releasing them could generate crucial new leads.
story: Dr. Kris Mohandie, a renowned forensic psychologist, breaks down the purported Nancy Guthrie ransom demands and shares his own take on what may have happened the night she was taken.

The two letters purported to be connected to Nancy Guthrie's suspected abduction leave investigators with questions about their authenticity, but forensic psychologist Dr. Kris Mohandie says investigators made the right call by releasing them because doing so could renew public interest and generate new leads.

"I don't think the ransom note is legit, and I don't think that that letter days later is legitimate — but I think it's appropriate for law enforcement to investigate it just in case it might be," he told Fox News Digital.
"A good investigation keeps an open mind," he said. "It really does."
NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM NOTES DON'T MATCH SUSPECT'S BEHAVIOR, PROFILER SAYS: 'I DON'T BELIEVE THEY'RE REAL'
A memorial to Nancy Guthrie in her hometown of Tucson as she remains missing. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

Some investigators said they were confident that the ransom demands are all bogus, while others are cautious about reaching that conclusion while Guthrie's whereabouts remain unknown, federal law enforcement sources told Fox News and Fox News Digital last month.

Early in the case, they appeared to have taken them seriously, with Heith Janke, then the special agent in charge of the FBI’s Phoenix field office, sitting down with Guthrie’s adult children, including "Today" co-host Savannah Guthrie, to record a video response to the first note.
Mohandie also cautioned against treating crime scene details in the first letter as proof its author was involved. Those include references to Guthrie's Apple Watch and a broken floodlight.
Nancy Guthrie, the mother of "Today" co-host Savannah Guthrie, remains missing, and the family is urging renewed attention as the search drags on. (Courtesy of NBC)

"I don't make much out of those two details," he said. "They seem to be details that inadvertently could have gotten to somebody, and so that's not enough for me to say, this is something only the killer would know."
NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM NOTES RELEASE FOLLOWS UNABOMBER ‘PRECEDENT' THAT CRACKED CASE, EXPERT SAYS

Mohandie said the letters also point to an author who appears comfortable with technology, citing references to Bitcoin, email communication and the unusual demand for "$4 million USD" — details he said could help identify whoever wrote the letters, whether they prove to be genuine or a hoax.

"I certainly question the legitimacy of the so-called ransom note in which the individual is sending it to a news outlet, saying this will be a ransom, so on and so forth, talks about ‘we’ and then breaks into ‘I’ in terms of pronouns," Mohandie told Fox News Digital. "There are a lot of things wrong with that ransom note, and it raised a lot of questions for me of veracity."
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

A pool service worker arrives at Nancy Guthrie's home in Tucson, Arizona, on Friday, March 6, 2026. Guthrie has been missing since the beginning of February 2026. (Matthew Symons for Fox News Digital)

Mohandie said he also has doubts about the second letter, which claimed Guthrie had "perished" days after the alleged kidnapping. While he said investigators are right to pursue every credible lead, he questioned whether a kidnapper would risk exposing themselves again with an apology or use the word "perished" in place of more common terms.
JUDGE ORDERS NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM IMPOSTER INTO INPATIENT TREATMENT BEFORE SENTENCING

"I understand why law enforcement needs to investigate these as potential leads, and it is a strategy that has worked," he said. "You look at Ted Kaczynski and putting that out there on the Unabomber case is what led to it being resolved. So they need to put that out there. Maybe somebody does recognize something unique in these writings."
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Even if the notes are hoaxes, investigators are looking to identify the sender and potentially bring criminal charges, as they did in the case of Derrick Callella, who sent "imposter" ransom demands to the Guthrie family in early February and has already pleaded guilty.
The devil is usually in the details.

However, he added, "the devil is usually in the details." And while much of the contents of the notes have been publicly known for months, the grammar and punctuation were only available to a select few before the Pima County Sheriff's Department made them public on Friday, July 31.
People bring flowers to Nancy Guthrie’s home in Tucson, Arizona, on Friday, March 6, 2026. Guthrie has been missing since the beginning of February 2026. (Matthew Symons for Fox News Digital)
PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF ISSUES ALERT FOR KIDNAPPING SUSPECT LESS THAN 10 MILES FROM NANCY GUTHRIE'S HOME

Mohandie said the surveillance footage released by investigators remains the most significant publicly known piece of evidence, adding that it appears more consistent with a burglary or home invasion than a sophisticated kidnapping plot.
GOT A TIP?

"Unfortunately, I think this case is a simple matter of a burglary gone wrong and then attempts to cover things up," Mohandie said. "But that's a hypothesis and good investigators are investigating all hypotheses and following leads, and I think they're doing their job here."

The only known suspect, the man who appears in the Nest doorbell video, remains unidentified. According to the FBI, he is roughly 5 feet, 9 inches to 5 feet, 10 inches tall with an average build. He was carrying a black Ozark Trail backpack.
Anyone with information is asked to dial 1-800-CALL-FBI or, to remain anonymous, call 520-88-CRIME.

The sum of all rewards in the case is over $1.2 million — none of which has been claimed.

title: Michigan military exercise preparing thousands of troops for changing battlefield
summary: More than 9,000 service members are training in Michigan under the Northern Strike exercise, which adapts to changing warfare, emerging technology and lessons from global conflicts.
story: More than 9,000 service members are training in Michigan as Northern Strike prepares U.S. and allied forces for an evolving battlefield.
GRAYLING, Mich. – Tanks fire across training grounds in northern Michigan as thousands of service members practice for a battlefield military leaders say is changing rapidly.

More than 9,000 participants from 36 states and territories and five international participants are taking part in Northern Strike 26-2, one of the nation's largest reserve-component military readiness exercises.
Northern Strike began in 2012 and is held twice a year. David Kennedy, a public affairs officer with the Michigan National Guard, said this summer’s exercise is the largest since it began.
Brig. Gen. Ravindra Wagh of the Michigan National Guard said lessons emerging from conflicts around the world are shaping how troops train.
US SAYS NORTH KOREA MISSILE LAUNCH POSES NO IMMEDIATE THREAT, 'CONSULTING CLOSELY' WITH ALLIES
A U.K. service member takes position during a practice attack at the Northern Strike military exercise in northern Michigan in August 2026. (Olivianna Calmes)

"You see what's happening in Ukraine right now. You see what's happening globally with some of our other emerging conflicts that you see," Wagh said. "And I think that this is a place where you can test and innovate."
Northern Michigan gives troops access to more than 200,000 acres of land, the Great Lakes and air, space and cyber capabilities.
The exercise also brings together different military branches and international forces to practice operating alongside one another.
A Paladin howitzer sits at a training area during the Northern Strike military exercise in Grayling, Michigan, in August 2026. (Olivianna Calmes)
"We want to train with the allies and partners we're going to go to war with," Wagh said. "We want our soldiers, sailors, airmen, marines to see it here. Figure it out here."
Fox News followed troops from the United Kingdom as they moved through a practice attack, one of several combat training exercises taking place during Northern Strike.
During another exercise, a crew inside a Paladin howitzer rehearsed a fire mission before moving on to live-fire training.
US ARMY OFFERING DEFENSE FIRMS 'CONCIERGE ACCESS' TO TEST WEAPONS AT MILITARY RANGES
Preparing for combat involves more than the troops on the front line. Northern Strike also puts the units responsible for keeping them supplied and supported through the same kind of training.
That includes the 445th Quartermaster Company, which runs shower and laundry operations.
A laundry operations station supports service members training during the Northern Strike military exercise in northern Michigan in August 2026. (Olivianna Calmes)

"Our main goal is to provide, I would say, logistical support and really strengthen the morale of the soldiers that are out there actually doing the big booms in combat," Company Commander Captain Kelson said.
For Pfc. William Flores, whose unit is from Trenton, New Jersey, the exercise offers a chance to practice before a potential deployment.
"This is like a practice run," Flores said. "So when we do get deployed, if we do get deployed, we are ready."
Technology is also changing the training.
Nearly 90 industry partners are participating in Northern Strike, according to Wagh, allowing troops to work with developing capabilities before potentially encountering them in conflict.
Soldiers rehearse a fire mission inside a Paladin howitzer during the Northern Strike military exercise in Grayling, Michigan, in August 2026. (Olivianna Calmes)

Those capabilities include autonomous resupply and drones used to deliver blood by air. Other drone systems can hover over a battlefield, assess casualties and relay information so medical resources can be directed where they are needed.
FORT HOOD SOLDIERS SHIFT TO UNDERGROUND TRAINING TO PREPARE FOR BATTLEFIELD MEDICAL CARE
3D printing is also being incorporated to produce parts and adapt capabilities.
"If you would have told me a few years ago, that'll be, you know, on the front lines, but we're doing it here," Wagh said.
Wagh said the speed of change is forcing the military to innovate more quickly and use exercises like Northern Strike to test those lessons before troops encounter them in combat.
A service member rests beside a military vehicle during the Northern Strike military exercise in northern Michigan in August 2026. (Olivianna Calmes)
"I hope they're a little bit better, a little bit more capable," Wagh said. "We want all of our units to have a higher, more capable state of readiness."

title: Two dead, including infant, after boat capsizes in New York Harbor; 12 rescued
summary: A 22-foot bowrider capsized near Liberty Island in New York Harbor Saturday night, killing an adult female and an infant, who were pulled from the water by NYPD divers.
story: A woman and child were killed after a boat capsized in New York Harbor Saturday night. (FNTV)
Two people, including an infant, died after a boat capsized near Liberty Island in New York Harbor on Saturday night, authorities said, and now the captain faces reckless endangerment charges.

The New York Police Department told Fox News Digital that officers responded to a report of an overturned vessel in the vicinity of Liberty Island at around 10:25 p.m. Twelve people were rescued from the water before police arrived, according to authorities.

A 27-year-old woman and five-month-old girl were later located in the water by NYPD divers. Both were transported to NYU Langone Hospital in Brooklyn in critical condition, where they were later pronounced dead. Their identities have not been released.
The boat captain, 46-year-old Manuel Hernandez of New York City, was arrested and charged with 13 counts of reckless endangerment, the Coast Guard said.
DRUNK REPEAT OFFENDER CALLED A 'TICKING TIME-BOMB' BEFORE 80-MPH BOATING COLLISION KILLED WOMAN: PROSECUTORS
A woman and child were killed after a boat capsized in New York Harbor Saturday night.  (FNTV)

"We are deeply saddened by the tragic loss of life last night, and our thoughts are with the victims' family and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time," said Captain Doreen McCarthy, Coast Guard Sector New York commander. "We are extremely grateful for the heroic, swift actions of our partner agencies and Good Samaritan vessel who assisted in rescuing survivors from the water. We are working closely with CGIS and the NYPD to investigate this incident. We are committed to holding illegal operators accountable to highest extent of the law to ensure the safety of everyone on our waterways."
The Statue of Liberty stands in the foreground as Lower Manhattan is viewed at dusk, September 8, 2016, in New York City. (Drew Angerer/Getty Images)
Police said some of the other passengers were also transported to the hospital and are believed to be in stable condition.
Authorities are investigating the cause of the capsizing and whether the vessel was an illegal charter.
A police source told Fox News Digital that the vessel was a 22-foot bowrider.
A man is treated after a boat capsized in New York Harbor, Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. (FNTV)
The NYPD's Harbor Unit, Scuba Team and Aviation Unit responded to the scene along with the U.S. Coast Guard.

title: Teen accused of killing 10-year-old cousin Lily Peters may avoid November trial after new hearing scheduled
summary: Carson Peters-Berger's resolution hearing is set for Aug. 26 in the Lily Peters homicide case, but questions remain about whether a trial will proceed.
story: Tanner Horner pleaded guilty to capital murder and aggravated kidnapping in the 2022 death of 7-year-old Athena Strand. (KDFW)
The Wisconsin teenager accused of killing his 10-year-old cousin, Lily Peters, in 2022 may not face a November trial after a resolution hearing was scheduled in the case.

More than four years after Lily's death, Carson Peters-Berger, 18, had been expected to stand trial in November on multiple charges, including first-degree intentional homicide and sexual assault, in connection with his cousin's death.
The Chippewa County District Attorney's Office announced that a resolution hearing has been scheduled for Aug. 26, according to WEAU.
NEW HAMPSHIRE SUPREME COURT OVERTURNS ADAM MONTGOMERY'S MURDER CONVICTION IN DAUGHTER HARMONY'S DEATH
Lily Peters was 10 years old when she was killed in Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin, in April 2022. (Chippewa Falls Police Department)
Chippewa County District Attorney Wade Newell told the outlet that the scheduled resolution means the case will not go to trial and will instead conclude following the hearing.
However, Peters-Berger's defense attorney, Michael Cohen, told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that the proceeding will "address issues in the case that will determine whether there will be a trial."
Court records do not yet indicate the nature of the resolution expected to be presented during the hearing later this month.
Lily was reported missing by her father on the evening of April 24, 2022, after she failed to return home from her aunt's house.
WASHINGTON FATHER ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY KILLING 4-YEAR-OLD SON AND BURYING BODY UNDER HIS HOUSE: REPORTS

Stuffed animals are left at the altar during a prayer vigil for 10-year-old Iliana "Lily" Peters at Valley Vineyard Church in Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin, on April 25, 2022. (Jeff Wheeler/Star Tribune via AP)
Her father later found Lily's bicycle in a wooded area in Chippewa Falls, but an initial search by police did not locate her.

Authorities were notified the following morning that Lily's body had been found near the area where her bicycle was discovered. Investigators said her injuries were consistent with blunt force trauma, according to the criminal complaint.
During an interview with police, Peters-Berger, who was 14 at the time, allegedly said he asked Lily to "go exploring off the trail."
According to the complaint, Peters-Berger allegedly "punched [Lily] in the stomach, knocking her to the ground" and struck her with a stick while they were in the woods.
TODDLER'S TRAGIC DEATH SPARKS MANSLAUGHTER CHARGES AFTER ALLEGED POISONING
Lily Peters, 10, was found dead near a wooded area in Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin, in April 2022 after being reported missing by her father. (Chippewa Falls Police Department)
Peters-Berger also allegedly told investigators that he strangled Lily and attempted to sexually assault her after her death, according to the complaint.
Afterward, Peters-Berger allegedly returned home, where "he showered and put his dirty clothes in the laundry," according to the complaint.

After learning Lily had been reported missing, Peters-Berger allegedly determined that "he needed to hide her better" and returned to her body, dragged her several feet and covered her with leaves, according to the complaint.

Peters-Berger was charged with first-degree intentional homicide, first-degree sexual assault and first-degree sexual assault of a child under age 13 resulting in great bodily harm. He faces life in prison if convicted of the most serious charge.

title: Florida man allegedly kills family's kittens in front of teenage daughter as form of punishment: officials
summary: Body camera footage shows deputies confronting David Charette Jr. after witnesses say he killed kittens to punish his teenage daughter in Lee County.
story: Bodycam video shows Lee County deputies arresting a Fort Myers father accused of killing two family kittens and injuring a third as a form of punishment against his teenage daughter, according to authorities.
A Florida father was arrested this week for allegedly killing the family's kittens in front of his teenage daughter as a form of punishment, authorities said.

Bodycam video released by the Lee County Sheriff's Office shows deputies responding to a home in Pine Manor after receiving a report that a man was attempting to drown and strike a 2-month-old kitten named Luna.
David Charette Jr., 48, was arrested and charged with aggravated animal cruelty after authorities accused him of killing two kittens and injuring a third.
Witnesses told deputies that Charette allegedly abused and killed the family's kittens in front of his teenage daughter as a form of punishment when she "acted up."
'DEEPLY DISTURBING' ANIMAL CRUELTY OPERATION INVOLVING BABY MONKEYS BUSTED BY ICE INVESTIGATION
Body camera footage shows David Charette Jr. speaking with Lee County deputies after authorities responded to allegations of animal cruelty at a home in Pine Manor, Fla. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)
Charette defended his treatment of Luna while speaking with deputies in the body camera video.
"The cat is in perfectly healthy condition," Charette told deputies. "I have to give the cat a bath because it soils itself in the cage."
"It's covered in crap and I have to give it a bath, and it cries, and she doesn't like that," he added.
Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno said the allegations involving Charette's daughter made the case particularly disturbing.
FLORIDA MAIL CARRIER ACCUSED OF SNATCHING PETS ON ROUTE, TRAPPING 100-PLUS CATS AND DOGS IN ‘HOARDING’ HOUSE
A 2-month-old kitten named Luna was taken to a local animal hospital for treatment and is recovering after an alleged animal cruelty incident, authorities said. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)
"A daughter says that when she acts up or when she's in trouble, her father kills her kittens. This is sickening to me," Marceno told CBS affiliate WINK.
Investigators said they later learned Charette had allegedly killed two other kittens over the previous year.
In June, Charette allegedly smothered a 1-month-old kitten with a bleach-soaked rag, according to the sheriff's office.
In a separate incident, investigators said Charette allegedly killed a 3-month-old kitten with a blow-dryer.
David Charette Jr., 48, was arrested and charged with aggravated animal cruelty after authorities accused him of killing two kittens and injuring a third. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)
Authorities said both kittens had been buried in the backyard, but investigators recovered only one during a search of the property.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Teen girls recall Jersey Shore ride malfunction that left them stuck hanging upside down
summary: Two 13-year-olds recall the terrifying minutes they spent stuck upside down on the Wipe Out ride at Castaway Cove in Ocean City, New Jersey.
story: Riders Charlotte Hacker and Emilia Gordon describe the terrifying moments they were stuck upside down on the Wipe Out ride at the Ocean City Boardwalk in New Jersey.

FIRST ON FOX: Early last month, on the day after the Fourth of July, more than a dozen people found themselves trapped upside down on a malfunctioning ride along the boardwalk in Ocean City, New Jersey.
Charlotte Hacker and Emilia Gordon, both 13, were among the passengers on the Wipe Out ride at Playland's Castaway Cove when it got stuck that evening.
The two friends were interviewed with their parents' permission, recounting to Fox News Digital the terrifying experience of dangling midair with no idea of when they would come down.

"We were stuck upside down for five to seven minutes, and it doesn't seem like that much to the people that were down watching us, but we were up there, and it felt like an hour," Hacker said on Saturday.
EIGHT RIDERS LEFT DANGLING ATOP 100-FOOT ROLLER COASTER FOR OVER THREE HOURS AT TEXAS AMUSEMENT PARK
The girls went to the boardwalk to celebrate Gordon’s 13th birthday, which was the following day. They said they often ride the attractions there and decided to try the Wipe Out because it was new.

The ride swings like a pendulum, repeatedly turning thrill-seekers upside down while its passenger compartment spins. Only this time, the ride inexplicably stopped with everyone suspended upside down.
"I seriously thought I was going to pass out," Gordon said. "You try to put your head up, but you literally can't. You can barely get it up at all."
The girls, seated next to each other, tried to carry on mundane conversations to distract themselves while blood rushed to their heads.
Visitors enjoy an evening on the Ocean City Boardwalk in Ocean City, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Drago/Getty Images)
SIX FLAGS GUESTS STRANDED 245 FEET IN AIR AFTER POWER OUTAGE FORCES COASTER EVACUATION
"I remember thinking that the lap bars were going to open and that we were just going to fall," Gordon said.
Family members on the ground waiting for their kids to get off the ride were terrified as well, the girls said.
"My uncle was there too, because we were all with my cousins, so he was also freaking out," Hacker said.
Eventually, the ride's operators managed to get it moving again, but to the girls' dismay, it kept on going. Once the ride finished, they said they weren't let off for another few minutes.
It is unclear what caused the apparent malfunction, and if any injuries were reported.
Charlotte Hacker (left) and Emilia Gordon (right) pose for a photo. The pair got stuck on an amusement ride in New Jersey in July. (Courtesy of Erica Hacker)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Hacker said the ride did not close, adding that there were some people who stayed in line and rode it after they got off.
"When we came off, people were literally clapping," Gordon said.
The amusement park offered ticket refunds to the girls, which they didn't think was sufficient after what they went through.
"That ride is five tickets, so they just gave back our ticket but [Hacker] only got three back. I got five. But still, after all that, I feel like you expect more," Gordon said.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Ocean City Fire Department, Ocean City Police Department, the ride's operator and the New Jersey Department of Community Affairs for comment.

title: Florida business owners allegedly scattered 1,500 mothballs on beach to send endangered birds packing
summary: Two St. Pete Beach business owners allegedly spread 1,500 toxic mothballs on sand to stop black skimmers from nesting and are facing felony charges.
story: Visit Florida President and CEO Bryan Griffin discusses the state's Great American State Fair exhibit, tourism industry and continued population growth on 'Fox Report.'

Two Florida business owners have been charged with third-degree felonies after allegedly spreading about 1,500 "toxic" mothballs across a beach in hopes of keeping an "imperiled" bird species from nesting there.
If convicted, they could each face up to five years in prison, fines of up to $5,000 and up to five years of probation.
The problem started in late April when beachgoers noticed mothballs on the white, sugary sand on St. Pete Beach in St. Petersburg, Florida.

Officers with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) and bird-loving volunteers from the Audubon Society mobilized. They plucked about 1,000 of the small, white orbs from the sand behind the Plaza Beach Hotel.
MASSACHUSETTS HOMEOWNERS STUNNED AFTER TOWN WARNS JULY 4 FLAGS THREATEN ENDANGERED BIRDS

Robert Czyszczon, left, and Christopher Monroe, right, were charged with third-degree felonies for allegedly scattering mothballs on a beach behind their businesses in St. Petersburg, Fla. (Pinellas County Sheriff’s Office)
Then 500 more appeared overnight.

The smelly balls containing pesticides dotted an area where endangered shorebirds known as black skimmers were "attempting to establish a nesting colony," FWC officials said at a news conference. Their placement also meant other wildlife and children "could easily come in contact with them."
It quickly became clear that someone might be targeting the birds, they said.
So FWC investigators flew into action.
Crying fowl
The discovery of the mothballs ruffled feathers in the community.
There was "a lot of public outcry," expressing concern for the birds, while investigators tried to locate the source of the mothballs, FWC officials said.
Law enforcement served search warrants, combed through "terabytes" of data and eventually seized cellphones to try to locate the individuals behind the caper.
That work led them to Christopher Monroe, owner and manager of Chris’s Beachside Bar, and Robert Czyszczon, owner of the Plaza Beach Hotel, FWC officials said.
Out of fear of lost revenue, the two allegedly hatched a plan to use mothballs to deter birds from congregating on the beach behind their businesses, authorities said.
HIKERS FACE $25,000 FINE AFTER OFF-LEASH DOG BARKED AT GRIZZLY BEAR ON BANFF NATIONAL PARK TRAIL
Officers with FWC worked with Audubon Society volunteers to remove mothballs from St. Pete Beach when they appeared in April. (FWC)

Through video surveillance and receipt records, investigators found that Czyszczon spent about $60 buying "a large quantity" of mothballs at a Walmart the day before they first appeared on the beach, FWC officials said.
Upon examining his phone, investigators found "incriminating" text messages between him and fellow business owner Monroe discussing their objections to the native fowl.
Text conversations revealed plans for placement of the mothballs on the beach, officials said. That’s what led investigators to Monroe as a suspect.
The men discussed how they "were going to do something" to prevent the birds from nesting on the beach, FWC officials said.
Black skimmers don’t nest in trees. They kick beach sand to make depressions on the ground. Then they lay their eggs and raise their young near the surf.
"They're the worst birds," one of the men allegedly wrote in anticipation of nesting season.
"The bird people will put up fence around the area, and then the beach people will not be able to get to and from because they will fence around that space."
Cellphone tower data showed Monroe’s phone was at the same location as Czyszczon’s phone on both nights when the mothballs appeared on the beach, FWC officials said.
The men feared that nests on the beach would lead to fewer customers and less money being spent there, authorities said.
"Why didn't you tell me we lose $25,000 to $50,000?" one allegedly wrote in a text.

Monroe and Czyszczon were charged with illegal dumping, a third-degree felony, according to Pinellas County court records. They also were charged with the "attempted take of a state-listed imperiled species by harassment," a misdemeanor, according to FWC officials.
Both are out of jail on bond.
MASSACHUSETTS HOMEOWNERS STUNNED AFTER TOWN WARNS JULY 4 FLAGS THREATEN ENDANGERED BIRDS
Black skimmers lay eggs in depressions they make in beach sand. (FWC)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
About 6,800 black skimmers live in Florida. FWC officials estimate that several hundred live on the beaches of Pinellas County.
SEND US A TIP

The pesticide in mothballs can harm people and wildlife that come into contact with their vapors, according to an educational publication by the University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (IFAS).

"With any pesticide, the label is the law," Brett W. Bultemeier, director of the UF/IFAS Pesticide Information Office, wrote in a 2021 educational publication about mothballs. "The label language is not simply a set of directions. Rather, they are requirements that are legally enforceable."

The birds probably weren’t hurt by the "harassment," FWC officials said.
But it did delay their nesting, they said. That pushes the date that their young can fledge from the nest further back in the season. And that could put them in danger.

A big storm at the end of hurricane season, which ends on Nov. 30, "can wipe out a colony if those young birds haven't fledged yet," an FWC official said.

An attorney for Czyszczon did not respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital. Court records indicate that Monroe doesn’t have an attorney. He couldn’t be reached for comment.

title: Cornell bans bear butchering after students carved up creature in dorm kitchen
summary: Cornell University now bans wild game processing in dorm kitchens after two students went viral for butchering a black bear in Ganędagǫ Hall.
story: A curious black bear pushed open the front door of a Southern California water district office, wandered inside to sniff around as stunned employees watched, then calmly let itself out and returned to the woods. (Crestline Village Water District)
Cornell University has added a new rule banning the processing of wild game in school kitchens, months after two students went viral for carving a bear in a dormitory kitchen.
"Processing wild/game animals in community kitchens is strictly prohibited," the school's new policy states.

The school confirmed to a student newspaper that the rule's addition was a direct response to the 2025 incident, which saw two students drag the carcass of a black bear they had killed into Cornell's Ganędagǫ Hall for preparation.
One of those students, Aaron Chin, revealed himself as one of the butchers on a podcast a few months after the incident.
CODY JOHNSON FIRES BACK AT CRITICS, CALLS ALASKA GRIZZLY BEAR HUNT A 'CONSERVATIONIST EFFORT'
Cornell introduced the new ban after an incident involving two students and a bear carcass in a campus dorm kitchen. (iStock)

Chin explained that he and his hunting partner, a fellow Cornell student, had planned on bringing the bear from the hunting grounds located roughly two hours from the school to a friend's house to prepare it, but claimed the friend had an emergency that left them unable to use his home.
Chin also said that, before bringing the bear meat on campus, he and his partner ensured they weren't breaking any campus rules.

"We were really diligent in reading all of the rules [and] regulations," Chin told the MeatEater podcast in September. "We made sure we did everything by the book because we knew we were going to be under scrutiny."

A man walks through the Cornell University campus Nov. 3, 2023, in Ithaca, N.Y. The school recently updated its campus laws to ban the processing of wild game after a pair of students carved a black bear carcass in a school kitchen in 2025. (Matt Burkhartt/Getty Images)
The incident incurred swift social media and on-campus backlash, prompting state regulators to investigate.
However, after an inspector from New York's Department of Environmental Conservation visited the kitchen where the carving took place, the agency found no code violations, according to an NBC report.

A California woman pleaded guilty to murdering her fire captain spouse last year, decades after she was convicted in the fatal stabbing of her former husband.

Yolanda Olejniczak Marodi, 54, pleaded guilty Tuesday to second-degree murder in the death of her wife, Rebecca "Becky" Marodi, 49, a longtime California firefighter who was found fatally stabbed at the couple’s Ramona home in February 2025.

Authorities found Rebecca Marodi, pictured, dead with multiple stab wounds.  (Cal Fire/Riverside County Fire Department)

She pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter in that case in 2003 before her release in 2013, according to the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation.
Marodi, a veteran Cal Fire captain, suffered multiple stab wounds during the Feb. 17, 2025 attack.

Prosecutors said surveillance footage captured her fleeing the home as Yolanda Marodi pursued her. Rebecca was found with several injuries to her neck, chest and back that authorities said were consistent with a stabbing.

title: Middle school student arrested after allegedly stashing homemade guns for robbery plot: sheriff
summary: Two Florida middle school students allegedly built homemade guns and explosives while researching mass school shootings, authorities say.
story: A Georgia judge sentenced Colin Gray to 15 years in prison after finding he ignored escalating warning signs and failed to remove his son's access to the rifle used in the 2024 school massacre.

A Florida middle school student was arrested and charged as an adult earlier this year after allegedly creating his own homemade guns and explosives in preparation for a robbery, authorities said this week.

The investigation into Julian Davis, 14, and his 13-year-old friend began April 27, when St. Johns County sheriff’s deputies received a tip that the boys had been messaging each other on Telegram about "holding someone at gunpoint" to rob them, according to an arrest report.
The alleged texts between the boys, who attended Switzerland Point Middle School, contained information about building a shotgun and musket and obtaining zip ties, according to the arrest report.

Sheriff Robert Hardwick and federal investigators addressed the case publicly for the first time during a news conference Friday. Authorities said charging Davis, who they claim demonstrated an intense interest in school shooters, could have prevented a "tragedy" at the middle school and the broader community.
A booking photo of Julian Davis, a 14-year-old middle school student who authorities say was planning an armed robbery with homemade guns. (St. Johns County Sheriff's Office)
UKRAINIAN NATIONAL WHO COMPLETED AIR FORCE OFFICER TRAINING CONVICTED IN GHOST GUN 3D PRINTING OPERATION

Davis was arrested April 30 and was charged as an adult with multiple gun and explosive offenses. Davis and his 13-year-old friend were both charged with conspiracy to commit a robbery with a gun. The younger boy was not charged as an adult.

Between April 27 and 30, sheriff's deputies and federal agents conducted multiple searches of Davis' home, finding three homemade firearms, ammunition, suspected explosive components and makeshift handcuffs.

Also found in Davis' home were handwritten notes depicting the construction of weapons and an apparent drawing of what appeared to be a Molotov cocktail, according to photos released by the sheriff's office.

Searches also revealed a tactical vest with "White supremacy drawings" and a copy of the manifesto by Brenton Tarrant, a White supremacist who, in 2019, went on shooting sprees at two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand, killing 51 people.
Homemade shotguns found in Davis' Florida home during searches by sheriff's deputies and federal agents in late April. (St. Johns County Sheriff's Office)
SAN DIEGO MOSQUE SHOOTING LEAVES 3 VICTIMS, 2 TEEN SUSPECTS DEAD, POLICE SAY

Other items of concern found by authorities in Davis' home included a U.S. Army improvised munitions handbook and a copy of "The Anarchist Cookbook," a 1971 book that contains instructions on how to make explosives, weapons and illicit drugs.
Hardwick said Davis and his friend had planned to rob someone named CJ, though investigators have been unable to determine who CJ is.
Based on this evidence, plus online searches by Davis, Hardwick said there was a "much bigger picture than just a robbery of that individual."
Ammunition found in Davis' home during searches by law enforcement officials. (St. Johns County Sheriff's Office)
NEW VIDEO SHOWS OKLAHOMA HIGH SCHOOL PRINCIPAL TACKLING GUNMAN WHO OPENED FIRE INSIDE THE SCHOOL

"Davis was using his devices in his home to research things. He had a [fixation] with people that had committed these mass school shootings, people that have gone in and done these mass stabbings," Hardwick said. "So, he was actually spending a lot of his time on there going through these high-profile cases. And it's something that he actually wanted to emulate."
Davis is still in custody at the St. Johns County Jail on $240,000 bond, the sheriff said. He pleaded not guilty to the charges against him and is scheduled to be arraigned again next month.

Davis' attorney, Jill Barger, expressed concern that Davis had spent four months "in an empty pod" at the jail. She told Fox News Digital he has grown frightened and depressed, while accusing the state of not providing him "the resources he needs."
Barger also slammed the sheriff's office for publicly announcing the charges, calling it an attempt to "influence jurors ahead of trial."
A photo released by the St. Johns Sheriff's Department of a homemade pistol and brass knuckles found in Davis' home. (St. Johns County Sheriff's Office)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Julian never even thought about harming anyone," Barger said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The police were reckless and cruel to suggest they prevented a mass casualty event. There is no evidence of this. No writings by Julian, no threats, nothing."
Davis' friend, with whom he was texting about the alleged robbery, spent 21 days in the Florida Department of Juvenile Justice before being released, the sheriff said.

Neither of the boys will be allowed to return to their school. St. Johns County School District Deputy Superintendent Paul Abbatinozzi clarified there was never a direct threat to Switzerland Point Middle School.

The tip about the boys' alleged activities was initially submitted to the school through FortifyFL, a platform created after the Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting designed to identify potential threats from suspicious students.

title: Teen accused of killing Citadel cadet and friend had lengthy rap sheet with few consequences, sheriff says
summary: The 17-year-old suspect in the DeLand double murder had charges dropped or dismissed repeatedly since 2021, Volusia County Sheriff Chitwood says.
story: DeLand Police Department Capt. Dice provides an update on the investigation into the shooting deaths of Citadel cadet Dustin Rose and his childhood friend, Samson Campbell, who were found in a vacant lot. The search for a suspect continues.

The teen accused of gunning down a Citadel cadet and his best friend racked up a rap sheet stretching back to 2021, authorities say, arguing he skated on charges again and again before the alleged double murder.

The DeLand Police Department in Florida said Dustin Rose, 19, and Samson Campbell, 18, were found dead at around 10:40 p.m. on July 29. Officials announced on Tuesday that an arrest warrant was obtained for a 17-year-old male arrested Wednesday by the U.S. Marshals Service.
During a news conference Wednesday, authorities said the three people "knew each other in some capacity," and said the teenager who was arrested has a "pretty good criminal history."

Childhood friends Dustin Rose, left, and Samson Campbell, right, were fatally shot in a vacant Florida lot. Police are searching for a suspect. (DeLand Police Department)

title: Actress convicted as accessory after double murder made disturbing remark before killings, former friend says
summary: Daniel Wozniak's ex-fiancée, Rachel Buffett, is explored in the true-crime series "A Killer Among Friends," and a former friend recalls chilling red flags.
story: A voicemail from Brian Walshe's mother offers new insight into the troubled marriage at the center of the high-profile Ana Walshe murder case.

A month before Juri "Julie" Kibuishi and Samuel Herr were murdered, Rachel Buffett was planning her bachelorette party when she encouraged a former friend to take ecstasy, according to the woman, Audrey.
"Well, if I slipped it in your drink, you wouldn’t know about it," Buffett told her, Audrey claimed.
Audrey, who also recounts the exchange in the Investigation Discovery true-crime series, "A Killer Among Friends," said it was the last straw.
SLAIN DAD'S DAUGHTER KNEW ‘BLACK SWAN’ EX-BALLERINA SHOT HIM AFTER ONE CALL: 'SHE KILLED HIM, DIDN'T SHE?'

Rachel Buffett, the former fiancée of convicted killer Daniel Wozniak, looks and listens along with attorney David Medina (right) as Junko Kibuishi, the mother of murder victim Julie Kibuishi, speaks in Orange County Superior Court just prior to sentencing in Santa Ana Nov. 8, 2018. Buffett was sentenced by Orange County Superior Court Judge Sheila Hanson to two years and eight months in jail for accessory after the fact. (Orange County Register)

"When Rachel and [her fiancé] would get mad at each other, and they were drunk, they’d yell at everyone," Audrey recalled to Fox News Digital. "Of course, he’s yelled at me when he was drunk before. But it wasn’t until that night that I decided to end our friendship."
Audrey said Buffett’s remark about secretly drugging her didn’t feel like an empty threat.
"I really believed Rachel would have drugged me at her bachelorette party because she thought it would be fun," she said.
Audrey, a former friend of Rachel Buffett's, speaks out in the episode "Staging a Murder" premiering Aug. 10, 2026, at 9 p.m. on ID. (Investigation Discovery)
Audrey walked away from the friendship. Buffett later reached out by text, inviting Audrey to be a bridesmaid and asking if she could come over.
About a month after Audrey ended the friendship, Kibuishi was found shot to death in Herr's apartment, while Herr was missing.

Buffett, an actress, was not accused of carrying out the murders or helping her then-fiancé, Daniel Wozniak, commit them. In 2018, an Orange County, California, jury found her guilty of two felony counts of being an accessory after the fact after prosecutors accused her of lying to and misleading investigators.

Rachel Buffett is the ex-fiancée of Southern California man Daniel Wozniak, who’s on death row for a double murder. (Investigation Discovery)
Fox News Digital reached out to Buffett for comment about Audrey's allegations. The case is explored in the episode "Staging a Murder" airing Aug. 10.

"Rachel and Dan loved each other, but they also got on each other’s nerves," Audrey said. "It was fine when they were sober, but then when they got drunk, they were always more aggressive. They would argue and fight. I remember one time when he was drunk, I yelled ‘F--- you’ to him, and I threw my shoe at him, hitting him in the back."

Senior Deputy District Attorney Matt Murphy alleged Rachel Buffett "lied, dodged questions and changed her story" while being interviewed by detectives who believed Daniel Wozniak was involved in two slayings. (Investigation Discovery)
Audrey’s friendship with the couple wasn’t always tumultuous. She met Buffett in college while they were studying theater.
"I just remember her being fun and bubbly," said Audrey. "I thought, 'That's the type of person I want to hang out with.'"
At a party, she crossed paths with mutual friends Kibuishi, a dancer, and Herr, a U.S. Army veteran.

Sam Herr was murdered May 21, 2010. He was 26. (Investigation Discovery)
"I just remember them being delightful, funny, warm and loving," said Audrey. "They were good people. You could tell they were good people."
The buzz among the friend group was Buffett's engagement to Wozniak, a community theater actor. They planned to get married on May 28, 2010. A week before the wedding, Kibuishi and Herr were killed.

Herr's father, Steve Herr, became worried because his son wasn't answering his phone and had failed to show up for a planned visit. He went to his son's apartment and let himself in. Everything appeared normal until he reached the bedroom and discovered Kibuishi's body. She was partially clothed and had been shot in the head. Herr was missing.
Steve Herr, Sam Herr's father, is interviewed in ID's "A Killer Among Friends." (Investigation Discovery)

"By then, I wasn’t invited to the wedding because I stopped being friends with Rachel and Dan," said Audrey. "I told her I didn’t want to be in the wedding. But when I heard the news, I was so confused. My brain couldn’t wrap around the idea of what happened.
"I thought, ‘What did they get themselves mixed up in?’" said Audrey. "Maybe they got drunk. Maybe they got blackout drunk."
Wesley Freilich, who knew Daniel Wozniak, spoke out about the case. (Investigation Discovery)
At first, police thought Herr had killed Kibuishi before fleeing. But that theory began to unravel when investigators discovered someone was still withdrawing money from Herr's bank account.

Raquel Herr, the mother of murder victim Samuel Herr, embraces Junko Kibuishi, the mother of murder victim Julie Kibuishi, outside the courtroom after Orange County Superior Court Judge Sheila Hanson sentenced Rachel Buffett, the former fiancée of convicted killer Daniel Wozniak, to two years and eight months in jail for accessory after the fact in Santa Ana, Calif., on Nov. 8, 2018. Police traced the transactions to teenager Wesley Freilich, who told investigators that Wozniak had given him Herr's ATM card and instructed him to withdraw money. Police arrested Wozniak at his bachelor party. After repeatedly changing his story during questioning, Wozniak confessed. Asked why he committed the murders, he replied, "Money and insanity."

"From what I found out, he was racking up tons of credit card debt," said Audrey. "That’s a poor excuse. There’s no excuse to do what he did."

"It’s a life-shattering thing to have happened. But then she responded, ‘You just want to talk to me because you want your five minutes of fame. You don’t really care about me.’

Junko Kibuishi, mother of murder victim Julie Kibuishi, speaks in Orange County Superior Court in Santa Ana, Calif., Nov. 8, 2018. (Mark Rightmire/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images)

"Is that what you are thinking right now?" said Audrey. "It was mind-boggling. There was such a disconnect. I was completely taken aback by that reaction. To me, that is not the reaction of a woman who just found out her fiancé was a murderer."

Buffett has maintained that she had no advance knowledge of the murders.

"We were close for so many years," said Audrey. "No matter what I thought, I was still going to treat her like a human being. At that point, it had only been a few months since we ended our friendship."

Orange County Senior Deputy District Attorney Matt Murphy speaks during a news conference as Steve and Raquel Herr, parents of murder victim Samuel Herr, listen after Orange County Superior Court Judge Sheila Hanson sentenced Rachel Buffett to two years and eight months in jail for accessory after the fact in Santa Ana, Calif., Nov. 8, 2018. "I’m innocent, and that’s what hurts me most in this whole situation is they’re trying to say I’m something I’m not," Buffett told NBC’s "Dateline."
In 2012, Buffett was arrested on suspicion of being an accessory after the fact. Prosecutors later said she lied to police and misled investigators while trying to protect Wozniak.

title: Moscow, Kyiv assassins hunt weapons bosses as Ukraine war spills beyond the battlefield
summary: Draganfly CEO Cameron Chell says drone company leaders are now primary targets as Russia and Ukraine race for battlefield AI and autonomy advantages.
story: Assassination attempts, car bombings and alleged spy plots put drone bosses in the crosshairs in Ukraine war, expert says.

A dangerous new front is emerging in the Russia-Ukraine war as attackers and alleged intelligence operatives increasingly target executives and engineers developing the cutting-edge drone technology that is reshaping the battlefield, industry experts warned Sunday.

The attacks include an Aug. 4 car bombing near Yekaterinburg that critically injured Vladimir Tkachuk, head of Russian drone manufacturer Uraldronzavod, and killed his driver, according to Russian state news agency TASS, The Associated Press reported.
His company produces the "Upyr," or "Ghoul," a first-person-view attack drone used by Russian forces in Ukraine.
'A NEW KIND OF WAR': INSIDE UKRAINE'S HIDDEN FACTORIES MASS-PRODUCING COMBAT DRONES

A car bombing near Yekaterinburg that critically injured Vladimir Tkachuk, head of Russian drone manufacturer Uraldronzavod, and killed his driver. (Valeriy Sharifulin, Sputnik, Kremlin Pool Photo via AP)

Days earlier, Andrei Cherezov, head of another Russian drone company, was shot three times in Tula overnight July 28-29 in an apparent assassination attempt, according to Ukrainian outlet Pravda. Authorities have not publicly attributed either attack to Ukraine.

Draganfly CEO Cameron Chell told Fox News Digital that the rise in attacks comes as Russia and Ukraine race for an edge in drone warfare, making the relatively small number of people responsible for developing new technology increasingly important targets.
"When you can't take out all the distributed infrastructure, drone manufacturing leadership becomes the primary target," Chell said.

"These strikes in Russia and Ukraine and Germany on founders, leaders, engineers of defense and, in particular, drone-type companies are down to drones and these companies having such an impact themselves."
UKRAINE’S BATTLEFIELD IS TRANSFORMING THE FUTURE OF NATO
Anti-drone laser system trialed on a Stryker combat military vehicle with a machine gun aimed at the sky in Ukraine during a counteroffensive. (Michelle Ursi/Getty Images)

"Because drone technology evolves rapidly — often with significant iterations occurring every 10 to 30 days — targeting a key engineer, founder, or product lead creates immediate operational disruptions on the battlefield."
"Taking out a particular engineer or taking out a particular leader can set a very important weapons program back quite some time and disrupt shipments to the front line," Chell added.

German authorities have also arrested two suspected operatives accused of spying on a Bavarian drone manufacturer for Russian intelligence, while reports this month said the alleged operation included preparations to target company executive Stefan Thumann, according to Germany’s Die Zeit.
The case follows a reported 2024 plot disrupted by U.S. and German intelligence to target Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger.
ZELENSKYY ANNOUNCES 'THE FUTURE IS HERE' AFTER WAR'S FIRST ALL-ROBOT CAPTURE
Drone components and battlefield systems assembled at a Ukrainian manufacturing facility in an undisclosed location in western Ukraine. (Efrat Lachter/Fox News Digital)
Chell said as Ukraine and Russia push toward artificial intelligence and autonomous weapons systems, engineers developing those technologies are more strategically important.
"What we see in the Ukraine-Russia conflict is nobody in the loop — total autonomy is the direction things are going because it moves with more speed and precision," Chell said.
"AI and total autonomy are the big innovations for the next 18 months, so a potential reason we could see more targeted activity against leaders is because Ukrainians have that technology advantage."
"Targeting small drone companies is a relatively easy operation compared to targeting individuals in state-run weapons programs," he said.
"It is a fairly inexpensive, low-risk tactic for intelligence agencies that yields an immediate impact on the battlefield, and that's why we've seen this tactic."
"It is a very interesting turn or tactic that's being played by both sides here."
Chell highlighted how Russia and Ukraine approach such plots differently.
"I wouldn't suggest one side has an advantage over the other in terms of tactics, but psychologically, it has a deeper effect on the Russian side," Chell said.
UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS
"The volume of drone advantage will remain with the Russians for the foreseeable future, but the innovation of drones, tactics, and technology lies with the Ukrainians right now."
"Ukraine faces an existential threat, so they are ready for anything. Their tactics tend to be much more blunt — a direct shooter in a hallway or a car bomb," he added.

"The Russian tactics tend to be much more state-organized, using old Cold War tactics: low-level contacts, extensive intelligence and surveillance ahead of time, and inserting into other countries like Germany," he said.
"The Russians have a long-standing, well-established intelligence infrastructure dating back to World War II and the Cold War."
TRUMP IS PROVING THAT THE WAY TO BETTER OUR MILITARY IS TO SECURE OUR SUPPLY CHAINS
A soldier launches an RQ-35 Heidrun drone used for reconnaissance and artillery fire correction in the Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine on Feb. 22, 2026. (Dmytro Smolienko/Ukrinform/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
As the drone manufacturing industry takes greater precautions, Chell maintained that threats against companies and individuals in the defense supply chain are receiving increased scrutiny.
"We are very cognizant of it, and we're in contact with the proper authorities to make sure we're taking precautions on both a cyber and physical level to ensure we're at less risk," he said.
"We certainly don't take anything for granted."

"There are training and programs in place to ensure executives have a level of safety, primarily around awareness, cybersecurity, and physical location protection," Chell added before stating that the attacks and attempted assassinations have "heightened the conversation around it."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"We as an industry are taking it with a measured amount more seriously," he said.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Israel's new $634M German-built 'doomsday' sub gives major boost to Iran deterrence
summary: The INS Drakon is the largest submarine built in Germany since World War II, carrying a $634 million price tag as Israel bolsters naval power.
story: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said Wednesday that an American submarine torpedo sank an Iranian warship in international waters in a first since World War II.
Israel has taken delivery of its most advanced and expensive submarine from Germany, expanding its fleet amid escalating regional threats, according to reports.

The handover of the INS Drakon is expected to significantly bolster Israel's underwater strike and reconnaissance capabilities, The Algemeiner reported. The warship had been scheduled to be delivered in 2025.

A statement following the submarine's naming ceremony in Kiel in 2024 said the INS Drakon is of the Dolphin AIP class and "equipped with unique systems, including groundbreaking technologies that expand the range of the IDF's capabilities across various arenas."

Built specifically for the Israeli Navy by Germany's ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems (TKMS), the submarine is said to provide a vital sea-based layer of "deterrence and retribution," amid the war with Iran, defense analysts say.

Dr. Ehud Eilam, an Israeli national security expert and former researcher for Israel’s Ministry of Defense, told Fox News Digital that maintaining a continuous undersea presence is paramount for the nation's national survival.
TRUMP ADMIN PITCHES 15-POINT IRAN PEACE PROPOSAL AS PAKISTAN OFFERS TO HOLD TALKS
Israel has officially received the INS Drakon submarine from Germany, the most advanced and expensive submarine ever delivered to the Israeli Navy. (Reuters)
"Some of them would have to be at sea, on high alert, around the clock, if Iran suddenly attacked Israel in such a way that would cripple the IDF, including its strategic capabilities," Eilam said.
"In such a drastic scenario, Israel’s submarine/s that would be at sea could respond," he added.
"Israel’s other submarines might be in Haifa harbor at the time. They might be attacked and unable to operate. This demonstrates how important it is to always have submarines at sea."
TKMS reportedly handed over the INS Drakon—the sixth Dolphin-class vessel and third modified Dolphin II-class submarine in Israel's fleet—at its shipyard in Kiel, Germany, in late July.
US MOVES AIRBORNE TROOPS, MARINES AS IRAN REJECTS CEASEFIRE, RAISING GROUND WAR POTENTIAL
Israeli military submarine near the coast of Haifa at the Mediterranean sea (REUTERS/Nir Elias)

Measuring more than 70 meters (230 feet) in length with a displacement exceeding 2,000 tons, the vessel is reported to be the largest submarine constructed in Germany since World War II, carrying an estimated price tag of $634 million, according to The Algemeiner.
According to Israeli outlet Ynet , Israel's Dolphin-class fleet also provides the nation with a critical sea-based second-strike capability in its defense program.
"Everything is going according to plan with the new program for Israel," TKMS CEO Oliver Burkhard told Ynet Global.
"That also applies to the handover of the last boat of the previous series, including the homecoming in Israel," he said of the expansive submarine program.
The INS Drakon’s arrival comes as Israel projects increasing military power across distant operational theaters, Eilam said.
TRUMP IS PROVING THAT THE WAY TO BETTER OUR MILITARY IS TO SECURE OUR SUPPLY CHAINS
Dolphin submarines were developed in Germany for Israel. (Amir Cohen/AFP via Getty Image)

"Israel has been acquiring submarines for several purposes. One of them is for deterrence and retribution, such as if Iran manages to develop nuclear weapons," Eilam said before adding that "Israel has to be ready."
While submarines on active deployment carry out intelligence and reconnaissance missions across the Mediterranean Sea, their primary objective remains readiness for "doomsday scenarios," Eilam noted.

"Israel’s new submarine is bigger than others, which suggests Israel wants to have more options, such as increasing the range of the submarine's missiles so they can reach every target in Iran, even if the Israeli submarine is in the Mediterranean Sea," Eilam said.

"That way the submarine does not have to get closer to Iran, which requires crossing the Suez Canal, and this could be very risky, if not impossible in some situations," he added. "The other alternative is to bypass all of Africa, which would take a long time."
