title: Russia deploys North Korean missile unit to Ukraine; Moscow-Pyongyang axis deepens: report
summary: A Ukrainian intelligence official says Russia is deploying a North Korean unit with up to 120 ballistic missiles in its war against Ukraine.
story: Fox News senior foreign affairs correspondent Greg Palkot discusses the Russian missile attack on the Ukranian capital of Kyiv. At least 17 people were killed as tension between the two countries continues.

Russia has begun deploying a North Korean missile unit equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers for use in its war against Ukraine, a Ukrainian intelligence official told told Reuters Wednesday.

The reported escalation marks a deepening military partnership between Moscow and Pyongyang, with around 90 North Korean personnel expected to be stationed in Russia's western Voronezh region to support the new unit, according to Andrii Cherniak of Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR).
Cherniak also claimed Pyongyang has already delivered a fresh batch of 40 KN-23 and KN-24 ballistic missiles to Russian forces, Reuters said.
RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE

Russia has reportedly begun deploying a North Korean missile unit equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers for use in its war against Ukraine. (Alexander Kazakov/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
Final details of the deployment are expected to be finalized during high-level talks next month.
The intelligence report follows a massive Russian barrage against Kyiv and the surrounding region Aug. 4.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Moscow launched 24 ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and 115 drones overnight, killing at least 17 people.
Zelenskyy argued more lives could have been saved had Western allies replenished Ukraine's depleted stockpiles of air defense interceptors.
Zelenskyy previously warned that Moscow had been preparing since June to receive additional North Korean military personnel in the Voronezh region, according to reports.
RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY
Russian President Vladimir Putin has deepened his defensive ties with North Korea's Kim Jong Un. (Getty Images)
Cherniak told Reuters a Russian strike in late July marked the first recorded use of North Korean ballistic missiles against Ukrainian targets since August 2025.
According to HUR estimates, Russia has received approximately 150 KN-23 and KN-24 missiles from North Korea since late 2023.
Military analysts say Russia is increasingly relying on ballistic weapons because they require advanced defense systems — such as the U.S.-made Patriot — to intercept.

The Washington-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) assessed that Russia is deliberately incorporating more ballistic missiles into its long-range strike packages to maximize pressure on Ukraine's limited air defenses.
ISW added that North Korea is gaining critical battlefield data from the conflict, allowing Pyongyang to refine its missile performance using Russian operational experience.
ALARMING MISSILE REPORT DRAWS FORCEFUL RESPONSE FROM TRUMP AS IRAN WAR TESTS AMERICA’S ARSENAL
North Korea has emerged as one of Moscow's key military allies. (KCNA via Reuters)
North Korea has emerged as one of Moscow's key military allies since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began.
Reuters reported that Pyongyang has supplied millions of artillery shells and previously sent 14,000 troops to Russia's Kursk region to counter Ukraine's 2024 cross-border incursion.
Cherniak also noted that roughly 9,500 North Korean troops are still in Kursk, though they are not engaged in active combat right now.

A report by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) states that, since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, North Korea has supplied Moscow with large quantities of artillery and rocket ammunition, cannon and rocket artillery systems and ballistic missiles.

The policy institute described the Russia-North Korea relationship as one of the "most consequential among the Axis" and the only partnership in which one member has deployed troops in combat to assist another.

title: Nuclear experts urge Trump not to let Iran steer talks away from regime's atomic threat
summary: Nuclear experts urged President Trump to keep Iran’s nuclear program at the center of talks, warning that the regime could seek sanctions relief before addressing remaining nuclear capabilities.
story: The FDD's Andrea Stricker says Tehran is seeking control of the strategic waterway and sanctions relief before addressing its enriched uranium and nuclear infrastructure.
As negotiations continue over the Strait of Hormuz experts are urging the Trump administration to keep their eye on the ball when it comes to the Iranian nuclear program.

On Wednesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reacted to news of reported comments from IRGC chief Ahmad Vahidi, warning that Israel would continue preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, with or without a diplomatic agreement.

The remarks in question by Vahidi, which were first seemed to be reported in 2025 in an interview with an Iranian-regime-linked outlet, went viral on Wednesday, but after further investigation they seem to have come from an interview when he was interior minister and an adviser to the IRGC.

He reportedly told ILNA that the country's official line was that building a bomb was not on the table but "Iran’s hand is open…Iran can take actions if has not taken until now," in an account published by Khabar online, and shared with Fox News Digital.
WHO IS AHMAD VAHIDI? IRAN’S NEW IRGC CHIEF TIED TO GLOBAL ATTACKS AND ‘DEATH TO AMERICA’ IDEOLOGY
A map shows damage to Iran's Fordow nuclear site after being struck by the United States in Operation Midnight Hammer on June 22, 2025. (Fox News)

In reaction to the remarks that were amplified by Israel’s Ch. 14 on X, Netanyahu said during his speech that, "Today, we heard the commander of the Revolutionary Guards, Vahidi, explicitly declare Iran’s intention to continue developing nuclear weapons — ‘continue,’ as he put it," Netanyahu said at a ceremony marking the reinterment of Shimon and Rivka Herzl, the grandparents of the founder of modern day Zionism, Theodor Herzl."
"Well, as prime minister of Israel, I too, am determined to continue — to continue preventing Iran from possessing nuclear weapons," he said.
Netanyahu praised President Donald Trump as Israel’s greatest friend in the White House and expressed appreciation for the two countries’ joint efforts against Iran’s nuclear ambitions.

"Israel’s existence is not subject to negotiation," Netanyahu said. "With an agreement or without an agreement, I am determined — we are all determined — to do whatever is necessary to ensure our security and our future."
NETANYAHU'S ISRAEL GRAPPLES WITH TRUMP-IRAN DEAL AS DETAILS REMAIN UNCLEAR
President Pezeshkian said Iran would rebuild the nuclear facilities targeted by the U.S. and make them stronger in 2025. (Iranian Presidency/Handout/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to a spokesman for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office for clarification of his remarks.

The comments came as nuclear experts urged Trump to keep Iran’s nuclear program at the center of negotiations, warning that Tehran could use the Hormuz crisis to secure sanctions relief and other concessions before addressing its remaining nuclear capabilities.
Trump told "Fox News at Night" Tuesday that military force remained an option if Iran abandoned the talks, while insisting Tehran could not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.

"If they back out again, they’re going to get hit really hard," Trump told Fox News’ Trace Gallagher. "They know that. They understand that. I have no choice. They can’t have a nuclear weapon. It’s very simple.
"The hard hit is yet to come, and hopefully we won’t have to use it."

Trump said negotiators held an "all-day negotiation" Tuesday and described the discussions as "very good." He has said the talks would initially focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz before turning to Tehran’s nuclear program.
TRUMP WARNS IRAN WILL BE HIT 'REALLY HARD' IF NUCLEAR NEGOTIATIONS COLLAPSE AGAIN
A satellite view of the Natanz nuclear facility and Pickaxe Mountain, near Natanz, Iran, June 30, 2026 (Vantor/Handout via Reuters)
Andrea Stricker, deputy director of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies’ Nonproliferation and Biodefense Program, said that sequence could play directly into Iran’s strategy.

"It is in the Iranians’ interest to steer the negotiations toward the issues that they most care about," Stricker told Fox News Digital, including securing major U.S. concessions over Hormuz and "maintaining control of that crucial waterway that has proven a lifeline for Tehran to survive this war."
She said Iran would also seek oil sanctions relief and potentially relief from all U.S. sanctions, before addressing the nuclear file.

"If Tehran is able to structure the talks that way — and I’m concerned that Trump appears to be going along with that approach — there may be little left in terms of leverage to get big concessions from the Iranians on the nuclear file down the line," Stricker said.

There is evidence that Tehran has sought to sequence the talks in its favor. Axios reported in April that Iran proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending the war before beginning nuclear negotiations, potentially reducing U.S. leverage over enrichment and Iran’s enriched-uranium stockpile.

President Donald Trump, right, speaks alongside Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a model of Air Force One on the table during a meeting in the Oval Office of the White House April 7, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
The Washington Post later reported that Tehran was focused on preserving its leverage over Hormuz rather than engaging deeply on major nuclear restrictions.

Kelsey Davenport, director for nonproliferation policy at the Arms Control Association, agreed Iran is seeking to capitalize on the leverage it gained by disrupting maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

"The current focus on the Straits of Hormuz is not surprising. Iran is looking to capitalize on leverage gained by disrupting maritime traffic through the waterway and test if Trump is willing to negotiate in good faith," Davenport told Fox News Digital.
TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE
Satellite imagery taken Jan. 30, 2026, shows a new roof over a previously destroyed building at Natanz nuclear site. (2026 Planet Labs PBC/Handout via Reuters)

She said Tehran understands that any durable agreement will ultimately have to address its nuclear program but said, "At the end of this conflict, Iran will still possess the capabilities necessary to build a bomb," Davenport said, "The relevant knowledge and nuclear expertise cannot be bombed away.

"Tehran retains key materials and technologies necessary to build a bomb," she added. "If left unchecked, the nuclear program will be a source of instability and renewed conflict, even if Iran does not resume more proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities."

A proposed agreement between Iran and Oman could give Tehran some control over ships entering the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, a senior Iranian source and two regional officials told Reuters Wednesday. One regional source described the arrangement as a concession that had already been made, although the precise meaning of Iranian "control" remained under negotiation.
Iran is also seeking fees from ships traveling through the waterway, according to Reuters, while Washington has opposed both Iranian control and mandatory transit charges.
Stricker said postponing the nuclear issues would allow the regime to preserve its remaining enriched-uranium stockpiles and avoid fully dismantling its nuclear infrastructure.
She said Iran also wants to avoid accounting for its past nuclear weapons-related work or committing to end uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing.
The Bushehr nuclear plant in Iran April 29, 2024 (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
"Leaving them as a last-order issue in the negotiations likely means that we will not see the Iranians make big concessions and make a solid nuclear deal," Stricker said.
Davenport said the administration should prioritize restoring access for inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency before beginning detailed nuclear negotiations.

"The IAEA has not visited key Iranian nuclear sites in more than a year," she said. "It remains unclear how much of Iran’s nuclear infrastructure remains and where any gaps might be in trying to account for Iran’s nuclear materials."

She said renewed inspections would give Washington a clearer picture of Iran’s remaining facilities and materials, while helping negotiators design a verification regime capable of addressing any gaps.
Davenport also recommended pairing sanctions relief with specific, verifiable Iranian steps rather than negotiating one sweeping package.
"A series of smaller deals could build confidence in the process," she said.
Stricker urged the administration to link every concession involving Hormuz, sanctions or the U.S. blockade to a measurable Iranian step on the nuclear file.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The U.S. military has been enforcing a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, even during the ceasefire. (U.S. Central Command)
"The best approach to ensure a solid deal is to make the nuclear issues just as important as the Strait of Hormuz, removing the blockade and other top Iranian priorities," she said.

title: Israeli President Herzog calls antisemitism a 'contamination of societies' as hate crimes surge
summary: NYPD data shows anti-Jewish incidents account for 56.9% of all hate crimes in 2026 as Israeli President Isaac Herzog warns antisemitism is a global contamination.
story: Israeli President Isaac Herzog says antisemitism is an "age-old plague" that harms entire societies, pointing to Holocaust denial and social media distortions as growing challenges. (Video: Yoav Dudkevitch for Fox News Digitial.)
Israeli President Isaac Herzog issued a stern warning about the global spread of antisemitism in an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital at his Jerusalem residence.
"Antisemitism is an age-old plague which should be dealt with by everybody, by all societies. It's not an Israeli issue or only a Jewish issue," he said.

"It's a contamination of societies that starts with the Jews — never ends with them. It's the most dangerous phenomena that has to be dealt with aggressively, with no mercy, with full adjudication, and most importantly, with education," he added.
EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN
Growing antisemitism and other issues led President Isaac Herzog to launch Voice of the People in April 2023. (Yoav Dudkevitch/TPS-IL for Fox News Digital)

Herzog's warning comes as newly released New York City Police Department (NYPD) data show anti-Jewish incidents accounted for 56.9% of all confirmed hate crimes since the start of 2026, even though Jewish New Yorkers make up only about 10% of the city's population.
Herzog pointed to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whom he accused of spreading hate and compromising the lives of New Yorkers.

"Mamdani does not respect my nation's right for self-determination — the Jewish people's inherent right to have a nation of their own. And he's basically spreading blasphemy, hate, antisemitic rhetoric. He should understand that he's risking his own citizens, he’s risking their safety, well-being and life," Herzog told Fox News Digital.
In a video posted on social media on July 21, Mamdani called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "a war criminal" and "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people."
Days later, Raul Morales, 51, allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing two men on Manhattan's Upper West Side, including one who was visibly identifiable as Jewish.
SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK
Members of the Jewish community view the scene of an antisemitic arson attack in the Golders Green neighborhood of north London, on March 24, 2026. (Henry Nicholls/AFP via Getty Images)

"We've seen the stabbing just a few days ago... just because somebody was dressed as an Orthodox Jew. This cannot be accepted in New York, which is a city that is dear to our heart, dear to Israelis, and dear to me personally," Herzog said.

More broadly, a report released last month by the J7 Large Communities' Task Force Against Antisemitism found that 20 people were killed in antisemitic attacks across seven countries outside Israel in 2025, marking the deadliest year for such violence in the Jewish diaspora since 1994.
The J7 comprises Jewish communities in the United States, Australia, Canada, Argentina, the United Kingdom, Germany and France.
People walk through Times Square during an anti-Israel rally on Oct. 4, 2025, in New York City. (Stephanie Keith/Getty Images)

According to the report, more than 23,000 antisemitic incidents were recorded across the J7 countries last year, representing a 97% increase in violent attacks and a 136% rise in overall incidents compared with 2022.

"Of course, Israel is doing its best, but it has to be an effort with governments all over the world, law enforcement agencies, educational systems and Jewish communities, which we care about a lot," Herzog said, in reference to confronting Jew-hatred.

Referencing a recent article by professor Niall Ferguson titled "The Death of History," he said, "How much TikTok or the social networks distort the facts of history? They negate the worst and greatest horror of humankind, the Holocaust. And that's why we have to stand up together and combat it," he told Fox News Digital.
Herzog stressed that misinformation spread through distorted and superficial channels makes it easy to smear Israel on social media, but that such narratives do not reflect reality.
GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS
Aerial view of Israel's Mediterranean coastal city Tel Aviv. (Menahem Kahana/AFP via Getty Images)
SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

"[Israel] is the place where the Startup Nation flourishes. This is the place where great ideas are given to the world and contribute enormously to the world in so many great fields, from health to energy, to science, to agriculture, to food security, to what not. There's a reason why Americans who visit our country, young Americans, fall in love with this country," he said.

Growing antisemitism, coupled with polarization within and between Jewish communities and a weakening sense of Jewish identity in some places, led Herzog to launch Voice of the People in April 2023. The initiative brings together a council of 150 emerging leaders — one-third from Israel, one-third from the United States and the remainder from around the world.
Leaders are selected through an algorithm from thousands of candidates and serve rotating terms of roughly two years, developing ideas to address challenges facing the Jewish world.

The initiative held an in-person kickoff summit in March 2025 in Haifa, featuring Herzog and bringing together all council members, reflecting his belief in building the next generation of Jewish leadership, which he described as one of his main tasks.

"I'm overjoyed by the great ideas I see and feel, and I hope that around November we will have a new registration starting for the next slot, the next cohort, and I invite as many Jewish friends to register," he said.
Amelie Botbol is a freelance field reporter based in Tel Aviv, Israel, who reports on Israel-related news.

title: Capybaras crash Brazilian lawmakers' voting session and steal the show
summary: Capybaras wandered through the front door of the Mato Grosso state legislature in Brazil, surprising lawmakers preparing for a vote last week.
story: A group of capybaras has been crashing into a Brazilian state legislature's voting sessions. (UGC via AP)
Brazilian lawmakers preparing to conduct official business found themselves sharing the halls of a state legislature with several uninvited — but unusually relaxed — guests.
A group of capybaras entered the Mato Grosso Legislative Assembly in Cuiabá on July 30, briefly drawing attention away from an upcoming vote as they explored the government building.
Video recorded by legislative staffer Nayara Bueno showed the animals moving calmly through the entrance while workers sought to steer them outside.
BLACK BEAR CAUGHT ON VIDEO WANDERING INTO CALIFORNIA WATER DISTRICT OFFICE AFTER PUSHING OPEN FRONT DOOR
A group of capybaras has increasingly been crashing into a Brazilian state legislature's voting sessions. (UGC via AP)
"They show up here quite often, so we’ve gotten used to seeing them," Bueno told The Associated Press.
The rodents' guest appearance did not cause any damage to the Mato Grosso state legislature, according to officials.
The animals appeared calm as they wandered through the front door of the local legislative building in Cuiaba. (UGC via AP)
The legislature borders a park that is home to wildlife, giving the animals easy access to the surrounding government complex.

Native to South America, capybaras are semiaquatic mammals commonly found around wetlands and other bodies of water. They are highly social, generally travel in groups and can reach weights of about 175 pounds.
ROGUE PARROT ATTACKS PLAYERS DURING BRAZILIAN U-15 SOCCER GAME-THEN COMES BACK AND DOES IT AGAIN
The legislative building is located near a park filled with wildlife, where the capybaras had wandered away from. (UGC via AP)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The world's largest living rodents have also become internet favorites, with social media users frequently highlighting their laid-back behavior around other animals and people.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Iran’s unseen supreme leader becomes weapon in escalating power struggle, experts say
summary: Iran's rival factions invoke Mojtaba Khamenei's name to attack opponents, but his prolonged public absence raises questions about who governs.
story: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reportedly submitted a letter of resignation to the Office of the Supreme Leader on ‘Fox News Live.’

Iran’s rival political factions are increasingly invoking the authority of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei to attack their opponents and protect their own positions, even as questions persist over whether he is actively governing the country, according to an Iran expert.
The internal struggle surfaced in two reports published by Iran International concerning Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s relationship with the new supreme leader.

In the first report, senior cleric Mohammad-Bagher Kharrazi, a relative of the Khamenei family by marriage, claimed Pezeshkian had repeatedly threatened to resign and was warned that his next resignation would be accepted.
IRAN EXPERT BRANDS ISLAMIC CENTER OF ENGLAND IRAN'S 'UK OFFICE,' URGES IMMEDIATE CLOSURE
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian speaks with Fox News Channel's Martha MacCallum during an interview on Sept. 25, 2025, in New York City. (John Lamparski/Getty Images)
"If he resigns one more time, I will approve it," Kharrazi quoted Khamenei as saying.

Pezeshkian’s office strongly denied the account. Mehdi Tabatabaei, the president’s deputy for communications and information, called the allegation "baseless and an outright lie," while another presidential advisor said Kharrazi had no contact with the supreme leader and was known for telling "strange stories."
Hours later, Iran International published a second report alleging Pezeshkian had met Mojtaba Khamenei only once, inside a vehicle with tinted windows at an undisclosed location in Tehran.

According to the outlet’s unnamed sources, the encounter lasted several minutes, the two men could not see each other and Pezeshkian was not permitted to shake Khamenei’s hand. The report alleged that the president later questioned whether the voice he heard had actually belonged to the supreme leader.
IRAN’S GOOD COP, BAD COP GAME IMPLODES AS EXPERTS WARN REGIME VIEWS US AS 'EVIL'
Masoud Pezeshkian, then a presidential candidate, waves as he arrives to vote at a polling station in Shahr-e-Qods near Tehran, Iran, on July 5, 2024. (AP Photo/Vahid Salemi)

The claims have not been independently verified. Pezeshkian previously described a substantially different encounter, saying publicly that he had spent approximately two and a half hours with Khamenei in a cordial atmosphere.

Kasra Aarabi, director of IRGC research at United Against Nuclear Iran, said the competing claims surrounding Pezeshkian and Mojtaba Khamenei reflected a deeper struggle inside what he described as an "Islamist oligarchic mafia system."

Under Ali Khamenei, Aarabi said, the supreme leader functioned as the system’s "godfather," arbitrating among rival Islamist factions and guaranteeing their access to power and money. His removal created a vacuum that Mojtaba Khamenei’s appointment was intended to fill, but the new supreme leader’s prolonged public absence has left rival factions uncertain about who is actually in charge.

"The very essence of this mafia system is built on a godfather," Aarabi said. "If the godfather is absent, whether because he is severely incapacitated or nonexistent, that vacuum… re-emerges between the various Islamist oligarchic clans."
Aarabi said those factions are not primarily divided by ideology.
"They’re not competing over ideology," he said. "They’re competing over raw power and economic interests."

In that environment, Aarabi said, Mojtaba Khamenei’s name has become a political instrument that competing factions can invoke to legitimize themselves, constrain their rivals or justify decisions whose true source remains unclear.
WHO IS AHMAD VAHIDI? IRAN’S NEW IRGC CHIEF TIED TO GLOBAL ATTACKS AND ‘DEATH TO AMERICA’ IDEOLOGY

People hold placards with an image of Iran's new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, and the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, during a rally in Tehran, Iran, March 9, 2026. (Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) Via Reuters)

"Mojtaba’s name is the glue that’s holding the system together right now," Aarabi said. "Each of these clans invokes his name to justify its existence, legitimize its position, and consolidate its place within this fragile system."
Exiled Iranian journalist Mehdi Ghadimi described the resignation claims as part of a recurring political strategy used by reformist administrations.

"This is a familiar cycle," Ghadimi said. "Whenever they feel that their usefulness to the supreme leader has come to an end, they start circulating these resignation rumors in an effort to build public sympathy and improve their image before being pushed aside."

Ghadimi said similar rumors surrounded former presidents Mohammad Khatami and Hassan Rouhani during the final years of their administrations. He argued that reformist-aligned media channels often continue circulating resignation claims even after a president’s office formally denies them, allowing officials later to portray themselves as having challenged the supreme leader.
On Mojtaba Khamenei’s status, Ghadimi went further than Aarabi, saying he did not believe there was "a functioning person by that name who is capable of thinking, making decisions or speaking."
"Either he is dead, or he is being kept alive in an extremely unstable and severely deteriorated condition," Ghadimi said.

Aarabi said the two reports illustrate that dynamic. A cleric opposed to or unaligned with Pezeshkian invoked Mojtaba Khamenei’s authority to weaken the president by claiming his next resignation would be accepted, while figures around Pezeshkian pushed back with an account portraying the president as having met directly with the supreme leader.

Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared in any publicly released video or audio recording since succeeding his father, according to Iran International. Iranian officials have offered conflicting accounts about how often senior government figures have met him.
Aarabi cautioned that using Khamenei’s name as a source of authority will become increasingly difficult if his public absence continues.

A composite image shows several Iranian leaders named in the State Department’s Rewards for Justice program offering up to $10 million for information on key figures tied to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), including Mojtaba Khamenei, top left. (State Department/Rewards for Justice; Khoshiran/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images)

"There’s only so many times you can use someone’s name without any proof of life that they actually exist," Aarabi said. "The longer Mojtaba is absent, the more questions develop over whether he is alive or able. And as soon as that doubt increases, you will see this infighting increase."

title: Ceuta migrant surge exposes Spain-Morocco tensions as Islamist groups reportedly seek to exploit border crisis
summary: Spain reports 72 deaths as the Ceuta migrant crisis deepens, with intelligence officials saying Morocco allowed border controls to gradually relax.
story: Thousands of migrants from Morocco pored over the country's border with Spain and into Spain's African enclave of Ceuta on July 30, 2026. (Reuters)

Thousands of migrants remained stranded in Spain’s North African city of Ceuta on Tuesday as the European Union offered emergency assistance to reinforce the enclave’s border and Spanish authorities investigated whether criminals or suspected jihadists used last week’s chaotic mass crossing to enter European territory.

Approximately 72,000 people entered Ceuta from Morocco, and about 70,000 have since returned, Spanish officials said Tuesday, leaving roughly 2,000 people in the small territory. Reception facilities remained overwhelmed as authorities struggled to shelter hundreds of migrant minors and determine the status of those who remained.

Local authorities were processing 862 migrant minors, who receive special protections under Spanish law and cannot be summarily returned. The Associated Press reported that children were begging for food or sleeping outside after the youth shelter became overwhelmed.
SPAIN DEPLOYS MILITARY AFTER THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS OVERWHELM BORDER ENCLAVE, AT LEAST 18 DEAD
Migrants who crossed into Spain return to Morocco from the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Bernat Armangue)

The EU offered Spain assistance, including emergency financial support, to strengthen protection of its external border in Ceuta, European Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner said Tuesday following an emergency meeting of the bloc’s ministers in Brussels.

Brunner said the unprecedented crossing was fueled by criminal smuggling networks and disinformation spread through social media, as Spanish authorities were examining whether known criminals or suspected jihadists exploited the scale and disorder of the crossing to enter Ceuta undetected.

Spain’s National Police and Guardia Civil were reviewing video of the crossings and checking people who remained in the territory against criminal and counterterrorism databases, according to El Confidencial, which cited Spanish Interior Ministry sources.
Map depicting Spain, Morocco and Spain's Ceuta, which borders Morocco. (2026 EarthStar Geographics, OpenMapTiles, OpenStreetMap contributors)

The Spanish outlet reported that authorities were searching for known criminals and possible jihadists who may have entered among the tens of thousands who crossed. Interior Ministry sources acknowledged that the sheer scale of the surge created a genuine infiltration risk, according to the report.

El Confidencial said the concern was heightened by Ceuta’s proximity to Fnideq, also known as Castillejos, a Moroccan border town that has figured in previous jihadist recruitment investigations. Authorities have previously dismantled extremist cells operating across the Ceuta-Fnideq border area, while hundreds of people from northern Morocco traveled to join ISIS and other terrorist groups in Syria and Iraq during the mid-2010s, the outlet reported.
TRUMP BLASTS SPAIN MIGRANT SURGE AS 'CATASTROPHE,' WARNS US COULD FACE WORSE IF DEMOCRATS REGAIN POWER
Escorted by the Spanish army, migrants who crossed into Spain return to Morocco from the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)
The crisis is also creating an opening for Islamist movements seeking to weaken confidence in Morocco’s government, according to Zineb Riboua, a research fellow at the Hudson Institute.

Riboua said in an article that Moroccan Islamists have spent years portraying the monarchy as overly secular and pro-Western, attacking its relationships with the United States and Israel and encouraging the belief that young Moroccans have little future at home.
At the same time, she wrote, Islamist voices have promoted an idealized image of Europe as a place where prosperity and legal status can be easily obtained.

Riboua said the Ceuta crisis allows those movements to transform public frustration over migration, unemployment and economic conditions into a broader political attack on the Moroccan state ahead of the national elections in September.
Evidence has separately emerged that the mass crossing was preceded by an extensive online mobilization campaign.
Migrants inundating Spain's Ceuta. (Faro de Ceuta via AP)

An open-source intelligence report prepared by Golden Owl Intelligence traced weeks of activity across TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, including misleading interpretations of Spanish immigration law and practical information about routes, meeting points and recommended crossing times.

The report estimated that the content generated more than 11 million potential impressions through posts, videos, comments and interactions. It also identified messaging groups administered through telephone numbers carrying Algerian international codes.

The campaign accelerated after Spain’s Supreme Court issued a July 8 ruling concerning the immediate return of migrants intercepted at sea near Ceuta and Melilla, according to the report. Simplified and misleading interpretations of the decision, combined with confusion surrounding Spain’s policy to regularize hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants, were presented online as evidence that people who reached Spanish territory would be allowed to remain and eventually obtain legal status.
The investigation documented the later circulation of maps, swimming routes, transportation information and suggested departure points as tens of thousands of people began moving toward the border.
MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM
Migrants wait outside Ceuta's temporary migrant center following mass crossings of migrants from Morocco into Spanish territory, in Ceuta, Spain, Aug. 3, 2026. (Pedro Nunes/Reuters)

Morocco’s Interior Ministry spokesman Rachid El Khalfi said at a news conference Sunday that the surge resulted from several overlapping factors, including the exploitation of digital platforms, misleading information, human-trafficking networks and inaccurate interpretations of legal and administrative developments.

Khalfi said the messaging created the false impression that the border was open and that people could reach European territory without legal consequences. He said Moroccan prosecutors had opened investigations to identify those responsible and determine the appropriate legal consequences.

Reuters and the Associated Press have independently documented cases in which online claims influenced people to travel toward Ceuta. Reuters interviewed a Moroccan teenager who said Instagram videos inspired him and his cousin to make the journey, while a Moroccan human-rights activist told the AP that social-media posts initially claimed the border was open and later promoted a misleading interpretation of the Supreme Court ruling.
The crisis has also placed Spain’s intelligence services and its relationship with Morocco under scrutiny.

El País and Cadena SER reported, citing officials familiar with Spain’s intelligence assessment, that Morocco did not plan the mass crossing but allowed it to unfold after border controls were gradually relaxed.
Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said Spain’s foreign intelligence agency had not warned him of an imminent surge of that magnitude.
WHITE HOUSE BLASTS SPANISH GOVERNMENT AS THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS SURGE FROM MOROCCO, EMERGENCY REQUEST DENIED

Moroccan security forces clash with migrants attempting to cross into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta near the town of Fnideq, on the Morocco-Spain border, on July 31, 2026. (Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP via Getty Images)

Morocco has denied deliberately orchestrating the crossing. Interior Ministry spokesman Rachid Khalfi blamed the surge on online misinformation, human-trafficking networks and distorted interpretations of Spanish legal and administrative developments, according to The Jerusalem Post. The ministry said Morocco remained committed to international cooperation against irregular migration and human trafficking.
Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares defended Rabat’s response, saying Moroccan authorities quickly provided police support and helped facilitate the return of most of those who crossed.

Juan Jesus Vivas Lara, president of the autonomous city of Ceuta, offered a sharply different assessment, telling El País that many Ceuta residents believed Morocco had allowed, if not orchestrated, the surge.
"Morocco has shown us that it isn’t reliable," Vivas said. "There’s no alternative but to put in place whatever means are necessary to ensure it cannot do this again."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Moroccan government for comment but did not receive a response by the time of publication.
Reuters and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Holy Land battle: Solomon's Pools become flashpoint in fight over Israel's biblical heritage
summary: Israeli officials say the ancient Solomon's Pools have fallen into disrepair under Palestinian Authority administration, raising concerns over preservation and biblical heritage.
story: Aerial video captures the sprawling 2,000-year-old reservoirs that once supplied Jerusalem with water and are now at the center of a dispute over preservation, heritage and sovereignty. (Video by Yehoshua Sigala.)

Built more than 2,000 years ago to supply Jerusalem with water, Solomon's Pools have become the center of a modern political dispute, with officials from the nearby Israeli town of Efrat accusing the Palestinian Authority of allowing the historic site to deteriorate after it was placed under Ramallah's jurisdiction following the 1993 Oslo Accords.

Most archaeologists date the construction of Solomon's Pools, three ancient reservoirs located between Efrat and Bethlehem, south of Israel's capital, to the Hasmonean period in the second century B.C. The reservoirs were built to supply water to Jerusalem during the Second Temple period. Herod the Great (37–4 B.C.) later expanded the system to provide water to his palace-fortress at Herodium.

"Solomon's Pools are not only the history of the Jewish people in the Land of Israel and the source of Jerusalem's living water, but also the future of Efrat in our ability to exercise our sovereignty, preserve Efrat's development space and sustain tourism for all religions in the area between Jerusalem and Hebron," Dovi Shefler, mayor of Efrat, told Fox News Digital.
EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN
An aerial photograph shows a water reservoir at the historic site of Solomon's Pools. (Hazem Bader/AFP Via Getty Images)

The three reservoirs collectively hold approximately 288,000 cubic meters of water, or more than 10 million cubic feet. They are fed by the Arrub and el-Biyar aqueducts, which, together with rainwater, historically supplied Jerusalem with water year-round. During the British Mandate, the pools underwent significant renovations and became known as "Jerusalem's beach" until the Oslo Accords.
Under the agreements, the West Bank was divided into Areas A, B and C. Solomon's Pools are located in Area A, which falls under Palestinian civil and security control.

Yonatan Marcus, chief of staff of the Efrat Municipality, told Fox News Digital that during the negotiations, then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin maintained that the pools would remain under Israeli control, alongside other archaeological sites of major Judeo-Christian significance such as Rachel's Tomb in Bethlehem.
However, during the mapping process, he said, the words "Solomon's Pools" remained within Area C on zoomed-out maps, while the reservoirs themselves ultimately mistakenly fell inside Area A.
TRUMP’S MASSIVE GOP FAITH BLOC RAISES RED FLAG ON IRAN DEAL: TRUST HIM, NOT HIS TEAM

Marcus said under Palestinian Authority control, things changed for the worse. "When you visit today, you can see that the place is neglected. Much of it has been destroyed. There are signs everywhere in Arabic stating that swimming is not permitted because the pools are filled with sewage water," he said.

He added that the sewage contamination was not natural, with wastewater deliberately diverted into the pools, replacing the fresh water that flowed there until the Oslo Accords. He said this occurred despite the PLO's commitment under the agreement to protect historical sites in Area A.
"Our main goal is to protect these magnificent pools. It's not just about Jewish history; it's about Judeo-Christian history and whoever believes in the people of the Bible who walked here," he said.

He described the reservoirs as the largest archaeological pools in Israel, saying they occupy a strategic location between the Western Wall and the Cave of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs along Route 60, known as the Biblical Highway.
Although the pools are located in Area A, Marcus said visits by Israelis take place only on coordinated tours secured by the IDF's Judea and Samaria Division, as permitted under the Oslo Accords.

He noted that visits by Israeli officials, including Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, have prompted improvements, saying the Palestinian Authority removed about 200 bags of garbage from the site following years of neglect.
CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM
Panoramic view of the Old City of Jerusalem, Israel, viewed from Haas Avenue in late afternoon. (Planet One Images/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)
"If the pressure of our coming here is going to make them take care of the site, then wonderful. In the end, our goal is for it to be preserved," he said.
Ahmad Fattouh, a spokesman for Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas's Fatah faction, rejected the allegations.

"It's absolutely audacious that the leadership of the colonial settlement of Efrat claims to be concerned about the condition of Burak Sulaymān's pools when they are the very reason behind its declining water levels," Fattouh told Fox News Digital. He said Israeli locals diverted the springs that feed the pools and argued that the Palestinian Authority has restored the site and developed it as a tourist destination.

Fattouh also accused Israeli officials of using the issue to justify taking control of the site, saying Smotrich's visit showed that the pools were not completely dry, contrary to claims by Efrat officials.

Solomon's Pools, a series of ancient reservoirs south of Jerusalem near Bethlehem, have supplied water to Jerusalem for centuries and are at the center of an ongoing dispute over heritage, sovereignty and preservation. (Yonatan Marcus/Efrat municipality )
Yishai Fleisher, international spokesman for Hebron, said the pools are akin to rediscovering a lost part of the Jewish Temple, as they supplied Jerusalem with water for some 2,000 years.

He said preserving the site begins with attracting visitors, producing educational videos, improving access along the new road from northern Efrat, hosting senior Israeli officials and establishing a permanent presence with cameras, patrols and farms.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Since the story started breaking, the P.A. is trying to build a mosque there. The goal of the P.A. is to stop Israeli presence in Judea and Samaria and the Land of Israel. They are not about developing anything for its own sake," Fleisher claimed to Fox News Digital.

Fleisher, who is an influential voice among the Israeli right, called for a radical change in policy. "What we really have to do is dismantle the P.A. and assert sovereignty over Judea and Samaria. In the meantime, the line should be redrawn so that Solomon's Pools, which are essentially archaeological sites, are placed under Israeli control in Area C," he said.
Amelie Botbol is a freelance field reporter based in Tel Aviv, Israel, who reports on Israel-related news.

title: How Spain’s migration surge tested E.U. border policy
summary: An unprecedented surge of migrants into Spanish territory of Ceuta in North Africa marked the first  reignited the European Union’s debate over immigration.
story: Tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, an autonomous Spanish territory in North Africa, between July 30 and 31. The unexpected crisis overwhelmed local authorities and infrastructure, marking a first test of the European Union’s (E.U.) new Pact on Migration and Asylum. The scale and speed of the crossing exposed a real flash point in Europe’s migration system, but how fast authorities regained control has become its own point of contention—over whether the E.U. system is failing or working as designed.

The surge drew criticism from Washington and European capitals. The State Department claimed that the Spanish government had led efforts “to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe.” Denmark and Italy led a similar critique at the E.U. level, sending a letter—co-signed by 22 member states—that called for coordinated E.U. border measures and accused Spain of enacting policies that were a “pull factor” for undocumented migrants. Far-right parties across Europe have seized on the crisis to attack Spain and Europe’s migration policy.

Charles A. Kupchan, an expert on European affairs at CFR, explained that the surge came as a shock because migration to the E.U. is generally “more of a trickle than a deluge” in terms of the number of arrivals. “This rush, this mass of humanity, all coming in the span of forty-eight hours is quite unusual, and it’s because of the size, scope, and speed that it caused such a stir,” he said.
While most migrants have since returned to Morocco, the incident has renewed the debate over European border and migration policy — long a thorny political issue.
What happened in Ceuta?

Approximately 72,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta from Moroccan territory in just a few days, according to Spain’s interior minister. (Some reports put this figure at between 50,000 and 60,000.) Most migrants reached Ceuta by sea, either by swimming or using makeshift flotation devices. More than 80 people died on both sides of the border, with many drowning or getting killed in stampedes.

title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
summary: Israel rejects Trump’s Gaza plan, Todd Blanche confirmed as attorney general, and a boat capsizes in the New York Harbor.
story: Israel will not accept the 15-point plan for Gaza set out by President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told a Cabinet meeting Sunday.

The peace plan called for a phased withdrawal of Israel’s troops from Gaza alongside the disarmament of Hamas, but Netanyahu said that Israeli forces are not going anywhere until Hamas completely disarms first.
Hamas had said last month that it would disarm, but only after Israel withdraws completely and stops all hostilities.

The explicit rejection of the plan, frequently touted by Trump as a key foreign policy achievement, also comes after months of growing tensions between the White House and Israel’s leadership over Iran.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google

There are no ongoing negotiations between Tehran and Washington, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday, after Tehran set out a series of steep demands for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, laid out the country’s conditions, saying it would not reopen the strait “until America corrects its behavior.”

The statement, as carried by Iranian state media, stated that the U.S. must withdraw its naval blockade, pay Iran damages for the war, unfreeze Iranian assets, lift sanctions on Tehran and permanently end the conflict against Iran and its regional allies.
The U.S. has yet to respond publicly to the list of conditions. Top officials previously ruled out making any immediate payments to Iran during past efforts to negotiate an end to the war.
Senate confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general
After weeks of uncertainty, Todd Blanche was confirmed as U.S. attorney general early Saturday in a mostly party-line vote.
Blanche, Trump’s former personal attorney, was confirmed by a vote of 50-49, with only two Republican senators, Susan Collins of Maine and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, voting against him.
The vote was held after 4 a.m. on Saturday, as a late-night session ran into the early hours ahead of a planned Senate recess.

Earlier Republican holdouts, Sens. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina, ultimately backed Blanche after receiving various assurances from the nominee, including an order rescinding the $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. (A legal loophole could still revive the fund, however.)

Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, confirmed Sunday that he spoke with Barack Obama following his primary victory last week and said he hopes the former president will join him on the campaign trail this fall.
“It was a really warm and inspiring conversation,” El-Sayed told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” about his call with Obama.

“I was grateful for his advice,” he added. “It was very warm, very inviting, and I know that he knows the critical role that Michigan is going to play in holding [President Donald] Trump accountable, in winning back the Senate and in building forward the future that we need.”

Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that embattled Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, who is facing abuse allegations, should drop his re-election bid and resign “if the allegations are true.”

Miller’s ex-wife Emily Moreno, the daughter of Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio, accused the congressman of domestic violence. Miller has not faced criminal charges related to the allegations and vehemently denied them, and he has vowed to stay in the race.

Boat captain arrested after vessel capsizes near Statue of Liberty, killing 2
A woman and her 5-month-old baby died after a boat capsized near Liberty Island in New York Harbor Saturday night.

The boat’s captain, 46-year-old Manuel Hernandez, was arrested and charged with reckless endangerment, the U.S. Coast Guard said. Investigators with the Coast Guard are coordinating with New York police to determine “whether the operation constitutes an illegal charter operation.”
The 27-year-old woman who died was identified as Queens resident Sara Sanchez and the baby was her daughter, Antonella Garcia, according to police.
Eleven other people were rescued and taken to area hospitals with minor injuries, according to the FDNY.
Perez Hilton in serious but stable condition and will need surgery
Perez Hilton was in serious condition Saturday at a Florida hospital after he livestreamed what appeared to be self-harm from his Miami-area home Tuesday night, his family said in a statement.
The blogger, known for celebrity news and criticism, has been stabilized, but his injuries will require surgery, the family said on Hilton’s website.
“He experienced significant blood loss and sustained additional injuries that will require surgery in the coming days,” it said. “His treatment and recovery will be a long process.”
The video appeared to show Hilton, 48, whose real name is Mario Lavandeira, covered in blood with visible cuts and holding what appeared to be a knife.

Dutch rider Demi Vollering won the Women’s Tour de France for the second time and in style by winning the ninth and final stage to extend her overall margin of victory.
A misdemeanor gun charge against All-Star Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden in Texas has been dismissed, court records show.
Louisiana health officials are urging residents to take precautions against a flesh-eating bacterial infection following the deaths of five people this year.
Don Nelson, the second-winningest coach in NBA history who won five championships as a player with the Boston Celtics, died at 86.

title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez says she hasn’t ruled out a potential run for president or Senate in 2028

Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in the Great Lakes State’s Democratic primary for Senate last week, overcoming the tens of millions of dollars spent by Stevens’ supporters to attack him.

title: ‘Highlander’ star Christopher Lambert leaves Pittsburgh fan convention early after health scare
summary: “Highlander” star Christopher Lambert left Pennsylvania’s largest comic-con early after reportedly collapsing at the event on Saturday.
story: “Highlander” star Christopher Lambert left Pennsylvania’s largest comic-con early after reportedly collapsing at the event on Saturday.

Lambert, 69, unexpectedly departed the convention due to a “personal issue,” Steel City Con announced on Facebook, adding that his photo-op had been canceled and his return time was yet to be determined.

TMZ reported that Lambert suffered a sudden medical emergency and collapsed while signing autographs, before being taken from the convention hall by ambulance. According to the outlet, Lambert’s representative said his blood sugar had dropped because he hadn’t eaten much that day.

The Pittsburgh-area convention, running Friday through Sunday, had shared a photo of Lambert posing with a fan at a meet-and-greet over the weekend, where he signed posters of himself as the immortal Scottish warrior Connor MacLeod from the 1986 cult classic “Highlander.”

Steel City Con initially said in a Saturday-night update that Lambert would return Sunday for more autographs and his delayed photo-op, but not his scheduled panel. On Sunday, however, organizers announced he would not attend after all.
“Christopher Lambert is unable to come today,” the convention wrote on Facebook. “He sends his regrets.”
Fans responded in the comments with well-wishes, saying his health and recovery come first.
Steel City Con and representatives for Lambert did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Lambert, who is best known for his iconic role in “Highlander,” rose to global fame in 1984 starring as Tarzan in “Greystoke: The Legend of Tarzan, Lord of the Apes.” He has also played the god Raiden in the 1995 film adaptation of “Mortal Kombat” and Methodius in 2011’s “Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance.”
Last year, the actor drew some ire from Sweden’s popular SciFiWorld convention after abruptly canceling his scheduled appearance there.
Lambert is expected to attend other conventions this month, including Fan Expo in Chicago next weekend and Mad Monster Expo in North Carolina the weekend after.

title: Sen. Jim Banks says Rep. Max Miller should drop his re-election bid if allegations are true
summary: The Indiana Republican is the latest GOP lawmaker to call on Miller, R-Ohio, to step aside in the wake of domestic violence allegations, which he has denied.
story: Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” Sunday that embattled Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, who is facing abuse allegations, should drop his re-election bid and resign “if the allegations are true.”

Miller’s ex-wife, Emily Moreno, the daughter of Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio, accused the congressman of domestic violence. Miller has not faced criminal charges related to the allegations and vehemently denied them and has vowed to stay in the race.

“The allegations against him are terrible, and if he’s endangering a seat in Congress as we’re trying to keep the majority in the House, and he should drop out if he’s endangering that seat,” Banks told “Meet the Press” moderator Kristen Welker. “He should drop out because of the allegations against him.”

The domestic violence allegations rocketed across the national political landscape after Miller posted a livestream denying them, prompting Sen. Moreno to publicly denounce his former son-in-law. Miller later called for the House Ethics Committee to investigate the allegations against him, saying he has “absolutely nothing to hide.”

Emily Moreno has accused Miller of throwing her against a wall, holding a gun to her head and throwing hot water on her, according to documents her lawyer released. Miller sued his ex-wife, alleging defamation, and her lawyers moved to dismiss the lawsuit. Sen. Moreno said in a statement this month that Miller “is a danger to my daughter, and I hold my breath every minute he has custody of my granddaughter.”
Asked whether he believed Miller should resign from office, Banks said, “If the allegations are true and watching this play out publicly, of course he should resign.”

“I don’t know enough about the political dynamics, but I’ve watched the allegations, they’re deeply troubling, and I pray for all involved, especially the kid, and hope that justice prevails in this case,” Banks said.
A spokesperson for Miller did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Banks is the latest Republican to publicly call for Miller to step aside. Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., called Miller “a degenerate sociopath” and said he should step aside. Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, has said that Miller “would be making the right decision to step aside as a candidate and resign from Congress to focus on what is in the best interest of his daughter.” Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., and Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., have told media outlets that Miller should resign.

A spokesperson for the office of the Ohio secretary of state has told NBC News that Monday is the deadline to replace a candidate. Miller was expected to headline an event in his district on Monday, but the Republican organization canceled the event days ago, citing security concerns.

title: Indian national arrested in Germany, charged with murder of Arizona girlfriend
summary: Varun Batchigari, 20, was arrested at an airport after, police believe, he fled the country.
story: An Indian national was arrested and charged with murder after fleeing the country as police investigated the death of his 19-year-old girlfriend in Tucson, Arizona.

Varun Batchigari, 20, boarded a flight to Germany at Tucson International Airport, en route to India, on Thursday — the day that Julissa Rubi Salazar was found unresponsive in her apartment near the University of Arizona, according to the Tucson Police Department.

Salazar’s family had requested a welfare check after being unable to reach her. First responders noticed indications of trauma upon arrival and called the police, who have not described Salazar’s injuries.
Batchigari was arrested upon arrival in Germany with the assistance of U.S. and German authorities. He was taken into custody on a warrant charging him with first-degree murder and kidnapping.
On Friday, he was awaiting extradition to Arizona.

title: Abdul El-Sayed says he hopes to campaign with Obama after ‘warm and inspiring’ call
summary: Top Democrats, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, have lined up behind El-Sayed after supporting his rival in the primary.
story: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan, confirmed Sunday that he spoke to Barack Obama following his primary victory last week and said he hopes the former president will join him on the campaign trail this fall.
“It was a really warm and inspiring conversation,” El-Sayed told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” about his call with Obama.

“I was grateful for his advice,” he added. “It was very warm, very inviting, and I know that he knows the critical role that Michigan is going to play in holding [President Donald] Trump accountable, in winning back the Senate, and in building forward the future that we need.”
Asked by “Meet the Press” moderator Kristen Welker whether the former president plans to join El-Sayed on the campaign trail this fall, the Democratic Senate nominee said, “I really hope so.”
El-Sayed on Tuesday narrowly beat Rep. Haley Stevens in the state’s Democratic primary for Senate, kicking off a fresh round of dialogue nationally about the future of the Democratic Party.

El-Sayed, a former county health department director, won the primary with the backing of several heavyweight national progressive figures including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif.

On Sunday, El-Sayed dismissed concerns about his support in Michigan after Stevens and state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who ran in the primary but suspended her campaign in July, drew more votes combined than the eventual Democratic Senate nominee in Tuesday’s primary.
“Five hundred thousand more Democrats voted than did Republicans in that election,” El-Sayed told Welker. “If that happens [in November], we are going to win in a landslide.”

“I know that we had it out with a very tough primary,” he continued. “There were a lot of issues that were discussed and differences that were identified and fixated on, but I will tell you this: that all of us agree that our differences are far smaller than what we agree on. And what we agree on is that Donald Trump has been an existential threat to our democracy.”

El-Sayed also drew scrutiny for his friendship and campaign appearances with progressive media figures like Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who previously said on a livestream that “America deserved 9/11.” Piker has since apologized for the remark.

On Sunday, El-Sayed called Piker’s comments about 9/11 “dumb” and said the resurfacing of those statements was “gotcha politics.” He didn’t commit to campaigning with or without Piker during the general election, instead saying that he’ll need a broad coalition of voters to win in November, including those who follow Piker.

“I’m less concerned now with who I’m campaigning with [and] a lot more concerned about who I’m campaigning to. We’ve got a lot of work to do to continue to build the coalition that’s going to beat Mike Rogers,” El-Sayed said.

He added, when pressed by Welker, “I think we have this notion sometimes on shows like this that we cannot or should not talk to certain groups of people, and I will tell you that the 3 million people who listen to Hasan are people I want to make sure understand that there’s a pathway into our politics around getting money out of politics.”

“I’m going to continue to have the conversations with those folks who we desperately need to reach out to. Just like I’m going to continue to have conversations with seniors in senior homes, folks up north, folks in Detroit, folks in Grand Rapids,” he said.

El-Sayed ran as an unabashed progressive, rejecting money from special interest groups during the campaign and pledging, if elected, to vote against support for Israel and in favor of “Medicare for All.”

Stevens, meanwhile, ran in the moderate lane, taking in tens of millions of dollars from industry groups and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC — a bipartisan group that backs politicians who support Israel. El-Sayed made Stevens’ support from AIPAC a cornerstone of his campaign against her, capitalizing on plummeting support for Israel’s government among members of his party.

The general election, where El-Sayed faces GOP nominee Mike Rogers in what is expected to be one of the most competitive Senate races this year, will be a major test of whether El-Sayed’s progressive brand of politics can win in a general election in a battleground state.

Republicans in Michigan and nationally have already begun to attack El-Sayed as a “radical” and “dangerous,” using his full name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, in videos released this week by the National Republican Senatorial Committee, Senate Republicans’ campaign arm.
El-Sayed characterized the attacks as similar to those from Republicans who have used Obama’s full name — Barack Hussein Obama — to attack him.
“We always knew they were going to go here. I mean, notice how they chose to use my full name in echoes to exactly what they did against President Obama,” El-Sayed told Welker.
“At the end of the day, it’s not radical to believe that people should be able to afford their groceries,” he added. “It’s not radical to believe that you should have healthcare in this country.”
Since his primary win on Tuesday, prominent Democrats who were skeptical of El-Sayed during the primary or endorsed Stevens quickly rallied around their party’s nominee.
On Wednesday, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said he had a “very good talk” that day with El-Sayed.

“I’m feeling optimistic about winning the Senate and with Michigan,” he added to reporters at the Capitol. “We are going to win in Michigan. We’re going to beat Rogers, and we’re going to take back the Senate.”
And on Thursday, Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, D-Mich., campaigned alongside her party’s Democratic nominees for statewide office, including El-Sayed.
Stevens, too, quickly backed El-Sayed this week after losing to him in the primary, telling NBC News’ “Meet the Press NOW” that there’s “no drama” between the two.

Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., who appeared later on “Meet the Press,” said he was excited to join El-Sayed on the campaign trail and that he expected that a lot of his fellow Senate Democrats would travel to Michigan this fall.

“I think you’ll see a lot of my colleagues in Michigan. I’ll be there supporting him because he’s presenting a strong contrast with a candidate who is pro-corporate, who is pro-Trump, who is pro-war,” Murphy told Welker. “I think he’s going to do incredibly well in that campaign.”

title: Boat captain arrested after vessel capsizes near Statue of Liberty, killing woman and her 5-month-old baby
summary: The captain was charged with reckless endangerment, officials said.
story: A woman and her 5-month-old baby died after a boat capsized near Liberty Island in the New York Harbor on Saturday night.
The boat’s captain, identified as Manuel Hernandez, 46, was arrested and initially charged with 13 counts of reckless endangerment, according to the New York Police Department and the Coast Guard.
Court records were not immediately available, and it was unclear Sunday whether Hernandez has an attorney. The New York County Defender Services did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Investigators with the Coast Guard are coordinating with New York police to determine “whether the operation constitutes an illegal charter operation,” the Coast Guard said in a statement Sunday.
The dead were identified as Queens resident Sara Sanchez, 27, and her baby daughter, Antonella Garcia, according to the NYPD.
It said both were taken to NYU Langone Health Brooklyn in critical condition and later pronounced dead at the hospital.
A 911 caller reported that the vessel, a 22-foot Bayliner pleasure craft, overturned in the harbor around 10:25 p.m. Saturday near Liberty Island, home to the Statue of Liberty, police said.
Bayliner makes a few 22-foot models, each with a capacity of 10 to 12 people, with its new V22 Bowrider able to carry a maximum of 12, according to its website.
Twelve people who were on the boat were rescued before police arrived and were taken to area hospitals with minor injuries, the NYPD said.
The mother and daughter were pulled from the water by police divers, part of an NYPD response that included a helicopter and its Harbor Unit scuba team, the NYPD said.
Neighbor Diego Naranjo, 35, said he met Sanchez a few months ago. She lived in New York City’s College Point neighborhood with the father of their children, he said.
Last week, he saw the couple bringing groceries home. On Sunday, he said, he spoke to family members who visited Sanchez’s home.
“She was a beautiful person, very kind, friendly, respectful,” Naranjo said in a phone interview.
Officials have not released details about the boat or its operator. The Coast Guard confirmed to NBC News on Sunday morning that the vessel was towed to shore and remains in police custody.
The Coast Guard has strict rules about charter vessels, their operators and renters, and the number of passengers on board.

“The Coast Guard, in coordination with the Coast Guard Investigative Service (CGIS) and the NYPD, is conducting an active marine casualty investigation into the circumstances and cause of a fatal vessel capsizing,” the Coast Guard said in its statement.

Liberty Island, on the New Jersey side of New York Harbor, is home to the Statue of Liberty, the iconic sculpture given to the U.S. by France as a symbol of the alliance between the two nations. The statue has been on the island since President Grover Cleveland dedicated it in 1886.
The island is a popular tourist destination, drawing visitors who climb to Lady Liberty’s crown for sweeping harbor views. Others opt for boat tours to take in the statue from the water.

title: Hunter Biden says Joe Biden’s cancer has spread
summary: Former President Joe Biden’s son, Hunter Biden, said his father’s cancer is spreading in what he described as a “very debilitating” state.
story: Former President Joe Biden’s son Hunter Biden told the BBC on Friday that his father’s cancer is spreading, describing it as “very debilitating” and “painful.”
“It’s really hard,” Hunter Biden told the British broadcaster about his father’s condition in a televised interview. “It’s really sad to watch.”

“I wish he would complain more, because it’s not good. The cancer has spread; it has metastasized into his bones and further. It’s very painful, and it’s very debilitating in many respects, but he’s still out there and he’s still doing his thing,” he added.
His remarks come after former first lady Jill Biden told NBC News in June that Joe Biden would live with cancer forever.

“He’s doing OK,” she told “TODAY” show co-host Craig Melvin. “I think if he had just been diagnosed with prostate cancer, that’s one thing because that can be cured, but the fact that it metastasized to his bones, that makes it a whole different story. And so I think Joe will live with cancer till the rest of his life.”
In May 2025, months after he left office, the former president’s personal office shared that he’d been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer.

In September 2025, the Biden family shared that Joe Biden had wrapped up a course of radiation therapy and hormone treatment, though it was unclear whether the former president would require more cancer care.
Last year, Joe Biden’s office also shared that he’d undergone surgery to remove cancerous skin cells.

Speaking to the BBC about his father’s cancer, Hunter Biden was emotional, telling the outlet: “He is our rock. He has been there for each one of us in a way that is hard for me to even possibly articulate and explain.”
In the interview, Hunter Biden also spoke about the pardon he was granted from his father just before he left office, which applied to any crimes committed from Jan. 1, 2014, through Dec. 1, 2024.
At the time, Hunter Biden was facing federal gun charges and had pleaded guilty to tax evasion charges.
On Friday, Hunter Biden said the pardon was “not fair” but added: “All I know is that I’m grateful that he did it for me.”

“It’s something that is easily criticized, and for good reason,” he said, adding later: “I was the only one in the world that could have gotten what I got from the only person in the world who could give it, my father.”
Previously, on California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s podcast, Hunter Biden said that his father’s decision to issue a pardon meant that the former president “chose me over his legacy.”

title: Sen. Jim Banks says Rep. Max Miller should drop his re-election bid if allegations are true

On Sunday, El-Sayed called Piker’s comments about 9/11 “dumb” and said the resurfacing of those statements was “gotcha politics.” He didn’t commit to campaigning with or without Piker during the general election, instead saying that he’ll need a broad coalition of voters to win in November, including those who follow Piker.

“I’m less concerned now with who I’m campaigning with [and] a lot more concerned about who I’m campaigning to. We’ve got a lot of work to do to continue to build the coalition that’s going to beat Mike Rogers,” El-Sayed said.

He added, when pressed by Welker, “I think we have this notion sometimes on shows like this that we cannot or should not talk to certain groups of people, and I will tell you that the 3 million people who listen to Hasan are people I want to make sure understand that there’s a pathway into our politics around getting money out of politics.”

“I’m going to continue to have the conversations with those folks who we desperately need to reach out to. Just like I’m going to continue to have conversations with seniors in senior homes, folks up north, folks in Detroit, folks in Grand Rapids,” he said.

El-Sayed ran as an unabashed progressive, rejecting money from special interest groups during the campaign and pledging, if elected, to vote against support for Israel and in favor of “Medicare for All.”

Stevens, meanwhile, ran in the moderate lane, taking in tens of millions of dollars from industry groups and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC — a bipartisan group that backs politicians who support Israel. El-Sayed made Stevens’ support from AIPAC a cornerstone of his campaign against her, capitalizing on plummeting support for Israel’s government among members of his party.

The general election, where El-Sayed faces GOP nominee Mike Rogers in what is expected to be one of the most competitive Senate races this year, will be a major test of whether El-Sayed’s progressive brand of politics can win in a general election in a battleground state.

Republicans in Michigan and nationally have already begun to attack El-Sayed as a “radical” and “dangerous,” using his full name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, in videos released this week by the National Republican Senatorial Committee, Senate Republicans’ campaign arm.
El-Sayed characterized the attacks as similar to those from Republicans who have used Obama’s full name — Barack Hussein Obama — to attack him.
“We always knew they were going to go here. I mean, notice how they chose to use my full name in echoes to exactly what they did against President Obama,” El-Sayed told Welker.
“At the end of the day, it’s not radical to believe that people should be able to afford their groceries,” he added. “It’s not radical to believe that you should have healthcare in this country.”
Since his primary win on Tuesday, prominent Democrats who were skeptical of El-Sayed during the primary or endorsed Stevens quickly rallied around their party’s nominee.
On Wednesday, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said he had a “very good talk” that day with El-Sayed.

“I’m feeling optimistic about winning the Senate and with Michigan,” he added to reporters at the Capitol. “We are going to win in Michigan. We’re going to beat Rogers, and we’re going to take back the Senate.”
And on Thursday, Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, D-Mich., campaigned alongside her party’s Democratic nominees for statewide office, including El-Sayed.
Stevens, too, quickly backed El-Sayed this week after losing to him in the primary, telling NBC News’ “Meet the Press NOW” that there’s “no drama” between the two.

Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., who appeared later on “Meet the Press,” said he was excited to join El-Sayed on the campaign trail and that he expected that a lot of his fellow Senate Democrats would travel to Michigan this fall.

“I think you’ll see a lot of my colleagues in Michigan. I’ll be there supporting him because he’s presenting a strong contrast with a candidate who is pro-corporate, who is pro-Trump, who is pro-war,” Murphy told Welker. “I think he’s going to do incredibly well in that campaign.”

title: A Hospital Patient Dreamed Of Attending A Metal Concert. So The Show Came To Him
summary: Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert but couldn’t leave the facility. So the show came to him.
story: Now *this* is metal.

Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert after receiving some difficult news about his health, clinical chaplain Roshene Lawson tells TODAY.com. While he was too medically fragile to leave the facility, Lawson pulled some strings to make magic happen.

With the help of staff and some kind folks at a local venue, Lawson threw a real metal show at the hospital in July, featuring band The Scepter, a whole lot of headbanging and, of course, that metalhead spirit.
Berry was able to rock out safely.

“Our clinical manager had told me he had some tears coming down during the concert,” Lawson says of Berry. “I went to ask him after. I said, ‘Were you crying because it was so loud?’ ... and he laughed and he said, ‘No, I’m really happy.’”

The Scepter played a 40-minute set for Berry, Lawson recounts. The band performed while fully decked out in their metal garb. They also set up their lights and blaring amps, along with some fans to blast their long locks, she says.
The Scepter’s Josh Collins explains that the band attempted to give Berry the most authentic experience they could.

“We wanted to give him a real show, not a watered down version because we were playing in a hospital,” he says. “It was emotional, for sure, but mostly we just felt privileged to be there and to play for him.”
Nurses painted Berry’s nails for the occasion and dressed him in a heavy metal shirt, Lawson adds. She even made tickets for the event, which patients used to attend the rock show.
“Everybody had to have their ticket to get in, and we tore the ticket, and they came in, and we had staff enjoying it with them,” Lawson says.

The chaplain explains that the idea for the concert came from a conversation she had with Berry after he was told about a change in his condition. She declined to disclose further medical details to protect Berry’s privacy.

“I went in and said to him, ‘Really, we can focus on this and how sad and frustrating it is, or we can focus on what you want to do with what’s left of life,’” Lawson recalls. “And he said, ‘I’d really, really like to go to a heavy metal concert.’”

Since Berry wasn’t cleared to leave the hospital, Lawson had to get creative. She called around and found Dominion Tavern, a spot that regularly hosts shows, and asked them for help. The business was more than happy to get on board, owner Scott McClinton says.
